Larkhollow rule — the five re-entry triggers, and what each affects:
What arrives
	What it affects
	A new application revision
	intake and completeness run again on the new revision; the prior revision stays in the file; any packet readiness bound to the prior revision is gone
	New evidence on an element — a reply, a reclassification, a corrected date
	that element re-opens; packet readiness is gone; other elements are untouched
	A credential expires or is renewed
	the licensure check re-runs on the new dates; a re-verification is placed in the file
	A decision that is not admissible, or that names a superseded revision
	nothing activates; the record is raised, kept, and never deleted
	A withdrawal by the applicant, or a discontinuation by the Clinical Director
	the file ends with the terminal reason recorded. It is never labelled appointed
	A re-entry adds an occurrence to the file. It does not overwrite the occurrence before it.

2. From the repository root, run:

   ```bash
   python3 -m credentialing run --batch inputs/batch-01 --sources sources --output deliverables --batch-number 1
   ```

3. Read the reported outcome, [run log](deliverables/run-log.md), and files listed in `produced`. Use the export date for business decisions; execution timestamps describe the run only.
4. Review working results, history and revision-bound evidence summaries. A queued notice is pending dispatch, not correspondence sent. Missing signatures, CV reconciliation, accreditation or referee provenance stay outstanding.
5. Run focused verification as documented in README. Compare real source records and independently check a calendar quantity. Report findings and limitations in `deliverables/verification.md`.
6. Stop at the owner gate. This invocation does not commit, seal, push, send messages or make reserved clinical/committee decisions.

What arrives
	What it affects
	A new application revision
	intake and completeness run again on the new revision; the prior revision stays in the file; any packet readiness bound to the prior revision is gone
	New evidence on an element — a reply, a reclassification, a corrected date
	that element re-opens; packet readiness is gone; other elements are untouched
	A credential expires or is renewed
	the licensure check re-runs on the new dates; a re-verification is placed in the file
	A decision that is not admissible, or that names a superseded revision
	nothing activates; the record is raised, kept, and never deleted
	A withdrawal by the applicant, or a discontinuation by the Clinical Director
	the file ends with the terminal reason recorded. It is never labelled appointed
	A re-entry adds an occurrence to the file. It does not overwrite the occurrence before it.

import copy
import unittest

from credentialing.revisions import assess_revision, verified_role


class RevisionTests(unittest.TestCase):
    def setUp(self):
        self.old = {"entry_id": "ENT-1", "application_id": "APP-1", "revision": "1",
                    "organization": "Hospital A", "role": "Staff Physician",
                    "supervisor": "Dr A", "contact_name": "Office A",
                    "contact_email": "a@example.invalid", "from_date": "2019-01-01", "to_date": ""}
        self.entry = dict(self.old, revision="2")
        self.reply = {"reply_id": "VR-1", "application_id": "APP-1", "entry_id": "ENT-1",
                      "attester_organization": "Hospital A", "received_from": "Medical staff office — Hospital A",
                      "verified_credential": "Employment — Staff Physician",
                      "requested_date": "2025-01-01", "received_date": "2025-01-15"}

    def assess(self):
        return assess_revision(self.entry, [self.old], self.reply)

    def test_unchanged_and_contact_only_can_reuse(self):
        self.assertEqual(self.assess(), {"changed_fields": {}, "missing_facts": [], "conflicts": []})
        self.entry.update(contact_name="Office B", contact_email="b@example.invalid")
        result = self.assess()
        self.assertEqual(set(result["changed_fields"]), {"contact_name", "contact_email"})
        self.assertEqual(result["missing_facts"], [])
        self.assertEqual(result["conflicts"], [])

    def test_changed_organization_old_source_conflicts(self):
        self.entry["organization"] = "Hospital B"
        result = self.assess()
        self.assertEqual(result["conflicts"][0]["verified"], "Hospital A")
        self.assertEqual(result["conflicts"][0]["declared"], "Hospital B")

    def test_changed_organization_equivalent_name_is_not_employer_proof(self):
        self.entry["organization"] = "Hospital B"
        self.reply.update(attester_organization="Independent CVO", received_from="Independent CVO")
        self.assertEqual(self.assess()["missing_facts"][0]["field"], "organization")

    def test_changed_role_requires_actual_role(self):
        self.entry["role"] = "Department Chair"
        result = self.assess()
        self.assertEqual(result["conflicts"][0]["field"], "role")
        self.assertEqual(result["conflicts"][0]["verified"], "Staff Physician")
        self.reply["verified_credential"] = "Employment verified"
        self.assertEqual(self.assess()["missing_facts"][0]["field"], "role")

    def test_changed_supervisor_is_not_attester_or_contact(self):
        self.entry["supervisor"] = "Dr B"
        self.reply.update(attester_name="Dr B", notes="Dr B signed this reply.")
        self.assertEqual(self.assess()["missing_facts"][0]["field"], "supervisor")
        self.reply["verified_supervisor"] = "Dr B"
        self.assertEqual(self.assess()["missing_facts"], [])
        self.assertEqual(self.assess()["conflicts"], [])

    def test_old_request_can_verify_revised_facts(self):
        self.entry.update(organization="Hospital B", role="Department Chair", supervisor="Dr B")
        self.reply.update(attester_organization="Hospital B", received_from="Medical staff office — Hospital B",
                          verified_credential="Employment — Department Chair", verified_supervisor="Dr B")
        result = self.assess()
        self.assertEqual(result["missing_facts"], [])
        self.assertEqual(result["conflicts"], [])
        self.assertEqual(result["changed_fields"]["role"]["evidence"][0]["source_ref"], "verification-replies.csv#VR-1")

    def test_explicit_role_does_not_silently_override_conflicting_credential(self):
        self.entry["role"] = "Department Chair"
        self.reply["verified_role"] = "Department Chair"
        self.assertEqual(self.assess()["conflicts"][0]["verified"], "Staff Physician")

            self.assertFalse(result['entry_checks'][0]['accreditation_verified'])

    def test_accreditation_notes_do_not_override_source_rejection_or_negation(self):
        for fact in ['The programme is not accredited.', 'Accreditation: unverified.',
                     'Accreditation: accredited pending confirmation.',
                     'It is not confirmed that the programme is accredited.',
                     'No source establishes accreditation; the programme is accredited.']:
            tables = copy.deepcopy(self.tables)
            next(row for row in tables['verification-replies'] if row['reply_id'] == 'VR-0101')['notes'] = fact
            self.assertFalse(self.residency_check(evaluate_replies(self.app(), tables, '2026-03-16'))['accreditation_verified'])
        tables = copy.deepcopy(self.tables)
        reply = next(row for row in tables['verification-replies'] if row['reply_id'] == 'VR-0101')

        self.assertFalse(self.residency_check(evaluate_replies(self.app(), tables, '2026-03-16'))['accreditation_verified'])

        self.assertTrue(check['accreditation_verified'])
        self.assertEqual(check['accreditation_source_refs'], [doc['path']])
        self.assertTrue(check['accreditation_evidence'][0]['accepted'])
        self.assertFalse(any(issue['detail'].startswith('ENT-0101: required accreditation') for issue in result['issues']))

    def test_accreditation_supplement_identity_source_and_negation_fail(self):
        for changes in ({'Application': 'APP-OTHER'}, {'Applicant': 'Someone Else'}, {'Revision': '2'},

        self.assertFalse(self.residency_check(self.evaluate_documents(self.supplement(

    def test_accreditation_supplement_receipt_window_and_index_availability(self):
        for received, index_date, before, expected in [

            ('2026-03-01', '2026-03-17', False, False), ('2026-03-16', '2026-03-16', True, False),
            ('2026-03-16', '2026-03-16', False, True), ('invalid', '2026-03-01', False, False),
        ]:
            fields = self.accreditation_fields()
            fields['Received date'] = received
            with self.subTest(received=received, index=index_date, before=before):
                doc = self.supplement(fields, index_changes={'date': index_date})
                self.assertEqual(self.residency_check(self.evaluate_documents(doc, before=before))['accreditation_verified'], expected)

    def test_accreditation_note_cannot_bypass_reply_receipt_window(self):
        for received, before, expected in [('2026-01-25', False, False), ('2026-03-17', False, False),
                                           ('2026-03-16', True, False), ('2026-03-16', False, True)]:
            tables = copy.deepcopy(self.tables)
            reply = next(row for row in tables['verification-replies'] if row['reply_id'] == 'VR-0101')
            reply.update(notes='Accreditation: accredited.', received_date=received)
            with self.subTest(received=received, before=before):
                result = evaluate_replies(self.app(), tables, '2026-03-16', before)
                self.assertEqual(self.residency_check(result)['accreditation_verified'], expected)

        docs = [self.supplement(self.peer_fields(number), path='letters/peer-' + number + '.md') for number in ('0', '1')]
        result = self.evaluate_documents(*docs)
        self.assertTrue(all(check['eligible'] and check['provenance_verified'] and check['usable'] for check in result['peer_checks']))
        self.assertEqual(result['peer_checks'][0]['provenance_source_refs'], [docs[0]['path']])
        self.assertFalse(any(issue['element'] == 'references' for issue in result['issues']))
        self.assertEqual(result['peer_checks'][0]['reply'], self.tables['peer-reference-replies'][0])

    def test_peer_route_record_cannot_resolve_ineligible_part_two(self):
        tables = copy.deepcopy(self.tables)
        next(row for row in tables['peer-reference-replies'] if row['reply_id'] == 'RR-0100')['related_or_partner'] = 'Yes'
        doc = self.supplement(self.peer_fields())
        check = evaluate_replies(self.app(), tables, '2026-03-16', documents=[doc])['peer_checks'][0]
        self.assertFalse(check['eligible'])
        self.assertTrue(check['provenance_verified'])
        self.assertFalse(check['usable'])

    def test_peer_return_record_rejects_wrong_identity_applicant_route_or_missing_method(self):
        for changes in ({'Application': 'APP-OTHER'}, {'Applicant': 'Someone Else'}, {'Referee': 'REF-OTHER'},
                        {'Reply': 'RR-OTHER'}, {'Received from': 'Applicant'}, {'Return method': 'telephone'},

        fields = self.peer_fields()
        fields.update({'Return date': fields['Received date'], 'Received date': '2026-03-10'})

# Scan an agent skill

Run a repeatable security check without copying the scanner or its dependencies into the workspace.
The wrapper uses [Cisco AI Skill Scanner `2.0.13`](https://github.com/cisco-ai-defense/skill-scanner/releases/tag/2.0.13),
released under Apache-2.0 at commit `ec7c7f09c38c30af00e145e113b69fae96cbeb1a`.

## Input

Require one local path: a skill directory, `SKILL.md`, or the lowercase `skill.md` used for a Fellow's
deliverable. Download a remote skill for inspection before scanning it; do not scan and execute a
remote repository in one step.

## Workflow

1. Run `scripts/scan.sh <path>` from this skill directory.
2. If the script reports that `skill-scanner` is missing, explain that installation downloads a large
   third-party Python dependency set and writes to the user's pipx tool environment. Ask before running:

   ```bash
   pipx install cisco-ai-skill-scanner==2.0.13
   ```

   If `pipx` itself is unavailable, stop and ask the user how they want Python tools installed. Do not
   choose a system-wide `pip` installation for them.
3. Re-run the wrapper after installation. Keep the default local-only scan. Do not enable LLM,
   VirusTotal, Cisco AI Defense, file uploads, or API keys unless the user explicitly requests and

name: kb-restructure
description: Rename, move, re-nest, or ARCHIVE a KB file/dir without breaking inbound refs — discover, classify live-vs-historical, execute, fix, verify (split/merge staged). Fire on any structural mutation ask.
argument-hint: "<operation: rename|move|re-nest|split|merge|archive> <target-path> [destination]"
---

# KB Restructure

> Operation-agnostic engine for structural mutations of existing KB content, plus one playbook per operation. Exists because ad hoc sweeps provably miss inbound references (hidden dirs, gitignored files, INDEX manifest rows) and text search cannot see symlink breakage at all. The engine is portable: it hardcodes no workspace paths and reads each workspace's own rename/move policy at preflight.

## Scope guard

- Mechanical structural mutations of EXISTING content only. Taxonomy redesign — new top-level structure, rethinking what goes where — is macro, human-owned (KB SOP principle: human controls macro; agents control micro). If the ask is a redesign, stop and surface it instead of executing. A user-requested mechanical rename/move of one existing node — root-level included — is in scope; redesign means changing the taxonomy's shape, not a node's name or location.
- One mutation per engine run. A follow-up mutation, even minutes later, is a new full run (see Gotchas).

## Inputs

- `<operation>` — `rename` | `move` | `re-nest` | `archive` (FULL) · `split` | `merge` (STUB — engine phase 1 stops on these)
- `<target-path>` — file/dir being mutated, KB-root-relative
- `[destination]` — new path (required for 1→1 operations)

Missing args → ask. KB root = walk up from cwd until the repository root (`.git/`). **Prerequisite: a git-managed KB** — root discovery, the clean-tree gate, history-preserving `git mv`, and the commit record all assume git; on a non-git tree, stop and say so.

## Engine (every operation runs these phases)

# Playbook — archive (1→archived)

Detailed steps for engine phases 2–9 when the operation is ARCHIVING: retiring content whose central thesis is dead or dormant, by relocating it into the host KB's archive container.

**Archive is not a move with a different destination.** The ref-mapping differs, and four of the 1→1 playbook's standing obligations INVERT. Read § Divergences before reusing any rename-playbook habit.

## Ref-mapping (1→archived)

| Element | Mapping |
|---|---|
| Live inbound refs | Re-point to the SUCCESSOR if one exists; otherwise keep the ref and add a supersession note (`[ARCHIVED: date, reason, superseded-by: path?]`). A ref with no successor is not deleted — a reader following it must land somewhere that explains the retirement. |
| The archived body | **Never rewritten.** Header tag only. Its internal path citations become frozen history the moment it is archived. |
| Old parent manifest row | **ANNOTATED, not removed** — the row records that the content existed and where it went. |
| Archive container manifest | A BATCH manifest is CREATED (host KB's convention — often a README, not the per-directory manifest file). |
| The archived node's own parent-pointer | **NOT repointed** (see § Divergences D3). |

## Divergences from the 1→1 playbook (each cost a real run)

- **D1 — The parent manifest row is annotated, not repointed.** A move says "the row follows the content." An archive says "the row records the retirement." Removing it erases the fact that the content ever existed at that location, which is the one thing a reader six months later needs.
- **D2 — The destination manifest is a BATCH manifest, not a directory manifest.** Archive containers group by batch (a dated, reason-slugged directory), and host KBs typically manifest a batch with a README carrying thesis + date + inventory + decision record — not with the ordinary per-directory manifest file. Read the host KB's existing batches and MATCH them; do not impose the 1→1 playbook's "create a manifest" reflex.
- **D3 — The archived node's own parent-pointer is NOT repointed.** The 1→1 playbook repoints it at the new parent. That is WRONG here: an archived manifest is part of the frozen record, and its pointer preserves where the content lived. Verify against the host KB's existing batches — if archived manifests there still name their pre-archive parent, preserve yours. (Confirmed on live content: the 1→1 reflex would have falsified the record.)
- **D4 — The body is frozen, but its OUTBOUND relative links still break.** Archiving usually changes ancestor depth (content descends into a dated batch directory). Every relative link INSIDE the archived content silently mis-resolves, with zero text change — and "never rewrite the archived body" appears to forbid fixing them. It does not: a link target is not body content. Recompute relative depth (rule below) while leaving prose, figures, and claims untouched. This is the single most-missed archive defect.

**D4 rule.** "Never alter an Immutable body" governs CLAIMS, not link RESOLUTION. Rewriting `../x` → `../../x` so it still resolves preserves the record; leaving it broken destroys it. Fix the depth; change nothing else. Record the link-depth fixes in the batch manifest so the edit is auditable.

## Steps

1. **Preflight.** As the 1→1 playbook (clean tree, scope statement, policy patterns, symcheck baseline). Additionally: read the host KB's EXISTING archive batches and record their conventions — batch-slug format, batch-manifest filename and shape, whether archived manifests keep their pre-archive parent-pointer (D3), whether a dormant batch carries a separate revival guide.
2. **Confirm the thesis is actually retired.** Archive is for retired/dormant content, not for content that is merely old or inconveniently placed. Relocating misplaced-but-LIVE content is a `move`, not an archive — dispatch the 1→1 playbook instead. If the host KB requires human approval for directory-level archiving, the engine FLAGS and stops; it does not decide.
3. **Discover.** Alias-form refscans exactly as the 1→1 playbook (full path always; basename always; ICASE / extension-less / URL-encoded per the host KB). Union the hit lists.
4. **Classify.** Verdict-log every hit per `classification.md`. One extra question per LIVE hit that the 1→1 playbook never asks: **does a successor exist?** Re-point live refs to the successor; where there is none, the fix is a supersession NOTE, not a re-point. Log which of the two each live hit gets.
5. **Execute.** History-preserving move into `{archive-container}/{batch-slug}/`, preserving the content's original relative layout below the batch directory. Add the `[ARCHIVED: date, reason, superseded-by?]` header to each archived file — header only, body untouched.
6. **Fix live refs** per step 4's re-point-or-note decision. Append-only operative records take append-fixes (never rewrite existing lines).
7. **Standing obligations** — none of these ever appears in the hit list:
   - Old parent manifest row → **ANNOTATE** (D1).
   - Batch manifest → **CREATE** per the host KB's convention (D2): thesis, date, reason, inventory, decision record, and any deliberate skips (e.g. Immutable bodies whose stale citations were deliberately left).
   - Archived node's own parent-pointer → **PRESERVE** (D3).
   - Stem-derived companions (sync snapshots, gitignored sidecars) travel WITH their main file. See § Companions.
   - **Outbound relative links inside the archived content** → recompute for the new depth (D4), then RESOLUTION-TEST each one.
8. **Symlink pass.** Whole-tree symcheck; delta against the preflight baseline must be empty.
9. **Verify.** Residue == logged leave-set. Every rewritten ref RESOLUTION-TESTED (a rewritten link is not a working link — see the 1→1 playbook's step-8 resolution gate). Plus the archive-specific gates:

Each gate is a COMMAND a fresh agent can run — not a description of one. `{area}`, `{batch}`, `{base-ref}` are yours to fill.

| # | Gate | Method |
|---|------|--------|
| 0a | **Decision record complete** | One row per decision unit; every verdict in the allowed set; every protected unit carries the protected verdict. A batch whose decision record is missing rows is a batch nobody can audit — and the rows you forgot are exactly the ones you did not think about. |
| 0 | **Protected paths still live** | `test -d` / `test -f` every path you promised NOT to touch. Run it FIRST — the cheapest way to catch a mutation that ran wider than its scope. |
| 1 | Live path vacated | `test ! -e {area}/{old-path}` |
| 2 | Batch complete | every archived unit present under `{area}/.archive/{batch}/` at its preserved relative path |
| 3 | File conservation | `git diff --name-status -M {base-ref}...HEAD` → renames only, **zero `D` entries** |
| 4 | No husk directories | snippet below — a directory left holding only a manifest and nothing else |
| 5 | No ignored-file leak | `leak="$(git diff --name-only {base-ref}...HEAD \| git check-ignore --stdin || true)"; [ -z "$leak" ]` — **`git check-ignore` exits 1 when NOTHING is ignored**, i.e. on the PASSING case, so a bare pipeline under `set -e` aborts on success. Capture the output and test it empty. |
| 6 | Headers + batch manifest | `[ARCHIVED]` header on every archived file; batch manifest present; Immutable bodies unaltered below the header |
| 7 | **Links resolve** | `scripts/linkcheck.sh <kb-root> <policy-file>` — compare against the pre-mutation baseline; the delta must be EMPTY (D4). **Status alone is NOT enough.** A checker that cannot RUN arrives as exit 1 under `set -e` (identical to "links found") and prints nothing, so a naive diff of two empty outputs reports clean. Assert the invariant: exit 1 MUST come with non-empty output, or the checker never looked. Use an ABSOLUTE path and an `[ -x ]` precheck. Covers both the archived content's own outward links and every inbound ref you rewrote. **A git-ref baseline compares TRACKED content only** — exclude gitignored trees from the delta or their pre-existing dead links all read as NEW. |
| 8 | Refs | `scripts/refscan.sh` per alias form → residue == the logged leave-set, set-equality both directions |

```bash
# Gate 4 — husk directories. TWO traps, both shipped live at least once:
#  1. `</dev/null` on the inner command: a command inside a read-loop that reads stdin EATS THE LOOP'S
#     OWN INPUT. (But NEVER put it on the loop's own input pipeline — that feeds the loop /dev/null and
#     silently disables it. Guard the commands INSIDE the loop, never the pipe feeding it.)
#  2. `if` — NOT `[ "$n" -eq 0 ] && echo ...`. A trailing AND-list makes the LOOP's exit status the
#     LAST iteration's test, i.e. "was the final directory a husk?" — so under `set -e` a normal tree
#     (last dir not a husk) returns 1 and KILLS THE GATE SCRIPT, skipping every check after it.
#     A gate that aborts on success is as useless as one that certifies on failure.
find {area} -type d -not -path '*/.archive/*' | while IFS= read -r d; do
  n=$(find "$d" -mindepth 1 -maxdepth 1 -not -name 'INDEX.md' </dev/null | wc -l | tr -d ' ')
  if [ "$n" -eq 0 ]; then echo "HUSK: $d"; fi     # NOT `[ ] && echo` — see below
done
```

**Negative-control at least one gate per run:** break one instance deliberately, confirm the gate goes RED, restore. **A gate never observed failing is not known to work** — and a gate that cannot fail is not a gate. Assert the POSITIVE end state, not merely the absence of the old string: "the parent row no longer names the old path" is satisfied by DELETING the row, which is failure mode 1. Compare SETS against a baseline measured on the SAME tree, never counts against a baseline from a different one.

## Links vs provenance strings (a blanket repoint corrupts the record)

Not every occurrence of an archived path is a link to fix. Distinguish:
- **Links** — a reader clicks them and expects to land somewhere. Repoint them.
- **Bare provenance strings** in citations ("sourced from `{path}`", a source column, a footnote) — they record WHERE a claim came from at a moment in time. A KB with several dated batches will contain provenance strings pointing into OLDER batches, and a blanket find-and-replace silently re-resolves them into the NEW batch. The citation then attributes a claim to a document it never came from. **That is corruption of the record, not a fix.**

Where provenance strings are numerous, leave them and add ONE banner to the containing doc explaining where paths of that era now resolve. One banner beats a hundred rewrites, and it cannot mis-attribute.

## Companions

A gitignored sidecar named from its main file's stem is a COMPANION and travels with it — the main file's reconstruction pointer breaks otherwise. This does NOT license touching a standalone confidential tree that merely happens to be gitignored: that is separate content with its own lifecycle, out of scope for any mutation of an unrelated file. The test is derivation, not ignore-status: does this file's NAME derive from the moved file's stem, or does the host KB declare it a companion? Yes → it travels. No → leave it where it is.

## Dormant vs dead

When the thesis is "de-prioritized, revival possible" rather than "disproven", the batch needs a second manifest — a REVIVAL guide — beside the inventory: what is in the batch, which parts are evergreen vs snapshot-stale (names, numbers, dates, org charts, regulatory citations all expire), the extraction pattern (copy out, strip the archived header, re-verify, re-file — never edit in place), and where any content that stayed live now lives. Cold-read it with a fresh agent before shipping: if a reader who has seen nothing else cannot re-enter the work from it, it is not done.

## Delegation

A scheduled archive sweep keeps DETECTION (what needs archiving) and ORCHESTRATION (cadence, batching, human approval gates, isolation, the PR). It delegates per-item EXECUTION to this playbook and carries zero copied procedure. Consumer skills reference this skill BY NAME, never by file path — plugin extraction moves paths.

## Failure modes this playbook exists to catch

| # | Failure | Caught by |
|---|---------|-----------|
| 1 | Parent manifest row deleted, erasing that the content ever existed | D1 / step 7 |
| 2 | Directory manifest imposed on an archive batch that wants a batch manifest | D2 / step 1 convention read |
| 3 | Archived manifest's parent-pointer repointed, falsifying the frozen record | D3 / step 7 |
| 4 | Relative links inside archived content silently mis-resolve after the depth change | D4 / step 7 + gate 7 |
| 5 | "Never rewrite the body" misread as "leave broken links" | D4 rule |
| 6 | Live refs blanket-repointed into the archive when a successor exists | step 4 successor question |
| 7 | Live refs with NO successor left dangling | step 4 supersession note |
| 8 | Archived body edited beyond the header tag | gate 6 |
| 9 | Live-but-misplaced content archived instead of moved | step 2 |
| 10 | Directory-level archive auto-executed without human approval | step 2 |
| 11 | Husk directory left behind | gate 4 |
| 12 | Delete+recreate instead of a history-preserving move | gate 3 |
| 13 | A green gate that never looked (scanner self-certifying) | step 9 negative control |
# Classification — live vs historical

Every refscan hit gets a LOGGED verdict before anything is fixed. Refscan hints are pattern-derived suggestions; the verdict is the agent's, made against this rule, one log row per hit.

Verdicts: **live** (fix per the operation's ref-mapping) · **historical** (leave alone — rewriting a point-in-time citation falsifies the record and is itself a defect) · **not-a-ref** (the text does not denote the target at all). The core test where no rule below decides: **is this text a pointer a reader follows today, or a citation of what was true when written?**

## Precedence — apply top-down, first match wins

0. **Identity screen.** Does the matched text actually denote the target path? A superstring path (`alpha/beta-archive/`), a same-named different file, or a coincidental string → `not-a-ref`, stop.
   **Syntax specimen = a PLACEHOLDER.** A path is a specimen only if it contains a metavariable a reader is meant to substitute (`{slug}`, `{{x}}`, `<name>`, `path/to/thing`) → `not-a-ref`; optional editorial refresh, not a ref-fix.
   **A CONCRETE path is a real ref — even if it is currently DEAD.** Do not use "it does not resolve" as a specimen test: a dead concrete path is a BROKEN POINTER, which is a defect to fix or log (playbook step 5), not a thing to ignore. (A live run's flagship template fix was exactly such a link — an Exemplar pointing at a real file via a wrong relative depth, dead for months. A "does-not-resolve → not-a-ref" screen would have left it dead, re-creating the very defect this skill exists to catch.) Nor is "it lives in a template" a test: templates carry real Exemplar links, "see also"s, and canonical-source references. **Placeholder, or it is a real ref.**
1. **Machine-regenerated bodies** (sync snapshots, compiled digests).
   **SCOPE — apply rule 2's container test FIRST. Rule 1 fires only OUTSIDE a frozen container.** A machine-derived body that sits INSIDE a frozen container (`.archive/` tree, workspace historical pattern) is FROZEN: `historical`, header tag only, body never edited — go to rule 2 and stop. (Scoped 2026-07-13: rule 1 sits above rule 2 in a first-match-wins lattice, so its DORMANT branch below was emitting `live` for machine-derived bodies that had ALSO been archived — and a dormant pipeline is exactly what an archived program has. That combination licensed editing a frozen archived body, which rule 2, kb-sop § Archive, and the archive playbook's gate 6 all forbid. Rule 2's only exceptions are rules 3, 4, and 5 — rule 1 is NOT one of them. NOTE the DORMANT branch is still the right call for a dormant program's digest that is NOT archived: dormant does not imply archived, and an unarchived derived body with a dead pipeline must be edited directly or its links rot forever.)
   Outside a frozen container, ask: does an owning pipeline re-derive this file's stale field? Three branches — a compiled file is not automatically leave-alone:
   - **A live pipeline re-derives it** → `historical (leave)`, note "regenerates via its own pipeline"; a forward pointer inside a generated body gets fixed in the SOURCE document, never the generated body — hand-edits break the pipeline's own drift detection.
   - **The compiled file IS the system of record** (a records/registry file) → `live`; direct edit IS the pipeline route; name the owning pipeline in the rationale.
   - **The pipeline exists on paper but is DORMANT or ABSENT** — nothing will actually re-derive this body (the program it serves is retired, the regenerator was never built, or it runs only on a trigger that will not fire) → `live`, direct edit; state WHY the pipeline is dead. A "Compiled" class label is a claim about how the file *should* be maintained, not evidence that anything still maintains it. Leaving a derived body's links dead because a hypothetical regenerator "owns" them is how a KB rots.
   - Pipeline CONFIG (frontmatter fields, registry entries) carrying the old path is always `live` — fix the config.
2. **Frozen containers**: `.archive/` trees, workspace historical patterns (loaded at preflight from the workspace's rename/move policy section), Immutable and append-only classes per the parent manifest → `historical` — INCLUDING manifests inside them: an INDEX.md inside an `.archive/` tree is part of the frozen record. Exceptions: rules 3 and 4 — **and rule 5**.
   **LIVE AUTHORITY WINS OVER A HISTORICAL PATTERN.** Before freezing, check the workspace policy's live-authority list (rule 5). A records file, a registry, or a live manifest that ALSO happens to sit under a historical pattern is still LIVE — freeze it and the KB's own system of record goes stale, which is worse than any over-fix. Policy patterns are coarse (a whole directory); the live-authority list is exact (a named file). Exact beats coarse. (A live workspace's coarse historical pattern for a transcript tree also matched the records file that the same policy names as live authority — freezing its own system of record.)
   **The manifest's CLASS field decides — not its prose description.** A manifest row whose *description* reads "archived research planning" while its *class* column is blank or Mutable does NOT freeze that directory. Read the class; check whether workspace policy names the path. If neither says frozen, the container is NOT frozen — fall through to rules 7-8 (host precedent first, then the core test) and judge the hits on their own merits. (A live run froze three files on a description alone; workspace precedent had in fact been fixing them. A directory whose name merely *sounds* retired — `.planning/`, `old/`, `legacy/` — is not a frozen container.)
3. **Navigation-pointer function test.** **SCOPE: this rule fires ONLY on a hit inside a FROZEN container (one rule 2 already froze).** It is the escape hatch out of rule 2 — nothing more. On a hit in an UNFROZEN container it does not apply at all; skip to rule 4. (Scoped 2026-07-13: as originally written its negative half — "body prose is a citation → historical" — silently fired on every unfrozen doc too, and since the lattice is first-match-wins it pre-empted rules 7-8 entirely, making them dead code. It froze exactly the files a live run had to fix.)
   **Append-only operative records are exempt from this rule.** If the frozen container is an append-only record (a log, a changelog, a run record — rule 4), a routing-shaped line inside it is STILL fixed append-only: add an old→new mapping line, never rewrite the existing one. Rule 4's entire purpose is that guard, and rule 4 sits BELOW this rule in a first-match-wins lattice — so without this exemption, rule 3 would emit `live, fix it` and the rewrite would falsify what the past run recorded. Same verdict, different fix: the fix is the point.
   **Machine-regenerated bodies are exempt from this rule, frozen or not.** If the hit sits in a body some pipeline re-derives (a sync snapshot, a compiled digest), a forward pointer inside it is fixed at the SOURCE and the body is never hand-edited — see rule 1. Rule 3 must never be read as licence to edit a generated body: a hand-edit there breaks the pipeline's own drift detection, and the next regeneration silently reverts you. (Restored 2026-07-13: scoping rule 3 to frozen containers accidentally dropped this, and a frozen snapshot containing "now lives at" then inverted to `live`.)
   Within a frozen container, for a NON-generated body: a line whose PURPOSE is routing today's reader OUT of the frozen record and onward to LIVE content — supersession headers, archive-README forward pointers ("Canonical:", "now lives at", "Relocated:", "superseded-by", a bare markdown link in a batch README pointing at the successor) → `live`; fix it even though its container is frozen. The label list is exemplary — function decides, not the label.
   **It must route OUTWARD.** A frozen manifest's own INVENTORY rows — the rows describing what sits beside it inside the batch — are not outward routing; they are the frozen record's description of itself, and they stay `historical` (this is what rule 2's "manifests included" means). The test: does this line send the reader to content that is still LIVE (→ fix it), or does it describe the frozen batch's own contents (→ leave it)? In-sentence mentions inside the frozen doc's body prose are citations, not routing → they stay `historical` (which is where rule 2 already put them; a dated briefing row-linked from a live INDEX keeps the doc reachable, but that does not make its inner narrative live — fix the INDEX row if the DOC moved, leave the prose). (Rule 1 cannot collide with this rule any more: rule 1 fires only OUTSIDE a frozen container, rule 3 only INSIDE one. A forward pointer inside an UNFROZEN generated body is rule 1's business — fix it at the source.)
4. **Append-only operative records** (error logs, changelogs, run logs that FUTURE runs consult as instructions) → `live`, but the fix is APPEND-ONLY: add an old→new mapping line; never rewrite existing lines.
5. **Live manifests and authority files**: INDEX.md (or equivalent) outside frozen containers; files the workspace policy names as live authority (records files, registries) → `live`.
6. **Sidecars** → `live`. A sidecar is a gitignored COMPANION whose name derives from its main file's stem (`{stem}.<class>.md` style) or that the workspace declares as a companion — it reconstructs its main file and must move with it (fix the reference AND physically move the companion). Every OTHER gitignored file is ordinary content: classify by these rules, fix its text in place, never relocate it just for being gitignored.
7. **Host-KB precedent** (checkable; use it before falling back to judgment). Does the KB's own record show how it classified THIS file — or this class of file — during a PRIOR mutation? Migration notes, historical-note blocks in manifests, and past batch READMEs routinely say so outright ("citations in X / Y / `dir/*.md` have been updated to point at the new paths"). If it does: **follow that precedent**, or overrule it explicitly and log why. A KB that treats the same file as frozen in one mutation and live in the next is incoherent in a way that neither choice alone would be — and the precedent is evidence about what the host KB considers a live pointer, which beats an outside guess. Absent any precedent, go to rule 8.
8. **Remainder** → judgment via the core test. The date on a document does not freeze it; what the path is DOING in the line decides:
   - **Communication / claim snapshots** (briefings, meeting notes, dated analyses, sent correspondence): body prose citing the old path is recording what was said or believed at a time → `historical`. Rewriting it falsifies the record.
   - **Working records of a program** (plans, progress logs, validation reports, deliverable inventories): the path is an ARTIFACT LOCATOR — it tells a reader where an output lives, and that output still exists under its new name. A reader follows it → `live`. The date stamps when the work happened, not what the file is called.
   - Where the two readings genuinely tie, prefer the one the host KB's precedent (rule 7) already chose; if there is none, prefer `historical` — over-fixing a citation is the more damaging error, because it destroys evidence, whereas a stale locator merely inconveniences a reader.
   - (Rule 3 is NOT in play here: it fires only inside a frozen container, and rule 8 is only reached for unfrozen hits. An unfrozen navigation line needs no exception — it is simply a live pointer.) Log verdict + one-line rationale.

## Self-reference

Two sources of designed self-hits. Both must be pre-logged BEFORE verify — an unlogged self-hit fails the residue gate.

1. **The run's own artifacts.** The verdict log and report cite old paths by design. If they live inside the KB tree, the verify-phase rescan hits them: pre-log each, verdict `historical`. (Better: keep them outside the tree, or `!`-exclude their directory in the policy file.)

2. **The run's own FIXES.** A correct fix routinely re-introduces the old path string. These are not residue to chase — they are the fix working as designed. Pre-log each. Four shapes, all observed in a single live run:
   - **Append-only mapping lines** (rule 4): the preserved original line still names the old path — that is the point.
   - **Strike-through resolutions**: a backlog or tracker item struck as done retains its original wording, old path included.
   - **Provenance notes**: an archive-batch manifest records what was migrated FROM.
   - **Migration / supersession notes**: a manifest or convention line that records the retirement necessarily names the retired path.

   The test: does this occurrence POINT a reader at the old location, or RECORD that the old location existed? Pointing → still a live ref, fix it. Recording → designed, log it and move on.

   **Verdict value for these rows: `live`.** They are hits that RECEIVED a fix — the fix simply happens to preserve the old string (that is what an append-only mapping line, a strike-through, or a provenance note IS). They are NOT `historical`: a historical verdict means "left untouched", and these were touched. They belong in the LEAVE-SET (the set of files that still contain the old path at the end) precisely BECAUSE their correct fix preserves it. Leave-set != historical + not-a-ref; see § Verdict log format.

## Verdict log format

| Path | Hint | Verdict | Rationale |
|---|---|---|---|

One row per hit; verdict values exactly `live` / `historical` / `not-a-ref` (append-only fixes are `live` with "fix: append" in the rationale). The log travels with the run report / commit body.

**The LEAVE-SET is not the same as the historical + not-a-ref rows.** It is every file that legitimately STILL CONTAINS the old path once the run is finished. That includes rows verdicted `live` whose correct fix PRESERVES the old string — an append-only mapping line (rule 4) keeps the original line verbatim; a strike-through resolution keeps the item's original wording; a provenance or migration note names what was retired. It also includes files the run itself CREATED. Build the leave-set explicitly, and gate residue as SET EQUALITY against it in both directions: an unlogged residue hit means a missed ref, and a leave-set file that no longer carries the old path means something was silently over-fixed. Both are failures.

- S uses schema version `credentialing-snapshot/1`, disallows additional properties and requires six element keys: `licensure`, `experience`, `gaps`, `education`, `certification`, `references`. Read S directly during implementation; these notes do not substitute for it.
- Every batch's caseload must appear, with latest applicable revision, status, all element states, readiness, cumulative received decision history, approval pointer, activation, conditions and owned actions. Action due dates may be null; monitored-condition due dates may not. Unknown is not zero, false or No. [R Snapshot contract; S]
- State history must include rejected evidence/decisions, attempts, prior revisions, readiness occurrences, outstanding work and awaited human events. A missing approval means null approval/activation, not an inferred decision. [R; P §§3,8–11]
- Status precedence is terminal (`withdrawn`, `discontinued`), then applicable missing-intake status, then the furthest applicable stage in S's order. Readiness remains independently computed; terminal/decision status alone cannot set it false. I3 20:34 permits disposition-resolved findings with readiness; I4 21:35 keeps unresolved discrepancies outstanding while retaining findings internally. [S application.status; P §8]
- Every run uses export date for business calculations. Execution timestamps belong in run logs/metrics. Snapshots link to prior snapshot path and exact SHA-256; first predecessor is null. The retained working state must agree with that predecessor. [R; S]
- Each refusal carries its real source decision ID and first failed condition, and survives future snapshots. Approval pointer must reference an admitted approval in the same application's decisions. Semantic checks must enforce this; schema validation alone cannot. [R; S; P §9]
- `produced` lists all files written/refreshed by that run, including snapshot and any working-state/history/run-log artifacts; `rules_file` must resolve. Record consumed documents and record files using office filenames. [R; S]
- Commit seals a snapshot. Preserve sealed bytes. A correction archives superseded occurrences unchanged, regenerates the changed and all downstream snapshots at standard paths, assigns new IDs, records supersession and commits a new chain. An unchanged rerun retains the sealed occurrence. [R Snapshot contract rule 6]
- Supported means all three batches and required artifacts complete and consistent; Partial requires a valid snapshot preserving unsettled scope with reason/owner; Blocked means the contracted batch result cannot be completed, including snapshot production after successful parsing; Deferred is a valid business hold. Diagnostic artifacts are not a Partial snapshot. A pending human decision alone need not imply a failed run. Record actual GB deferral separately from a generic waiting action. # Playbook — archive (1→archived)

Detailed steps for engine phases 2–9 when the operation is ARCHIVING: retiring content whose central thesis is dead or dormant, by relocating it into the host KB's archive container.

**Archive is not a move with a different destination.** The ref-mapping differs, and four of the 1→1 playbook's standing obligations INVERT. Read § Divergences before reusing any rename-playbook habit.

## Ref-mapping (1→archived)

| Element | Mapping |
|---|---|
| Live inbound refs | Re-point to the SUCCESSOR if one exists; otherwise keep the ref and add a supersession note (`[ARCHIVED: date, reason, superseded-by: path?]`). A ref with no successor is not deleted — a reader following it must land somewhere that explains the retirement. |
| The archived body | **Never rewritten.** Header tag only. Its internal path citations become frozen history the moment it is archived. |
| Old parent manifest row | **ANNOTATED, not removed** — the row records that the content existed and where it went. |
| Archive container manifest | A BATCH manifest is CREATED (host KB's convention — often a README, not the per-directory manifest file). |
| The archived node's own parent-pointer | **NOT repointed** (see § Divergences D3). |

## Divergences from the 1→1 playbook (each cost a real run)

- **D1 — The parent manifest row is annotated, not repointed.** A move says "the row follows the content." An archive says "the row records the retirement." Removing it erases the fact that the content ever existed at that location, which is the one thing a reader six months later needs.
- **D2 — The destination manifest is a BATCH manifest, not a directory manifest.** Archive containers group by batch (a dated, reason-slugged directory), and host KBs typically manifest a batch with a README carrying thesis + date + inventory + decision record — not with the ordinary per-directory manifest file. Read the host KB's existing batches and MATCH them; do not impose the 1→1 playbook's "create a manifest" reflex.
- **D3 — The archived node's own parent-pointer is NOT repointed.** The 1→1 playbook repoints it at the new parent. That is WRONG here: an archived manifest is part of the frozen record, and its pointer preserves where the content lived. Verify against the host KB's existing batches — if archived manifests there still name their pre-archive parent, preserve yours. (Confirmed on live content: the 1→1 reflex would have falsified the record.)
- **D4 — The body is frozen, but its OUTBOUND relative links still break.** Archiving usually changes ancestor depth (content descends into a dated batch directory). Every relative link INSIDE the archived content silently mis-resolves, with zero text change — and "never rewrite the archived body" appears to forbid fixing them. It does not: a link target is not body content. Recompute relative depth (rule below) while leaving prose, figures, and claims untouched. This is the single most-missed archive defect.

**D4 rule.** "Never alter an Immutable body" governs CLAIMS, not link RESOLUTION. Rewriting `../x` → `../../x` so it still resolves preserves the record; leaving it broken destroys it. Fix the depth; change nothing else. Record the link-depth fixes in the batch manifest so the edit is auditable.

## Steps

1. **Preflight.** As the 1→1 playbook (clean tree, scope statement, policy patterns, symcheck baseline). Additionally: read the host KB's EXISTING archive batches and record their conventions — batch-slug format, batch-manifest filename and shape, whether archived manifests keep their pre-archive parent-pointer (D3), whether a dormant batch carries a separate revival guide.
2. **Confirm the thesis is actually retired.** Archive is for retired/dormant content, not for content that is merely old or inconveniently placed. Relocating misplaced-but-LIVE content is a `move`, not an archive — dispatch the 1→1 playbook instead. If the host KB requires human approval for directory-level archiving, the engine FLAGS and stops; it does not decide.
3. **Discover.** Alias-form refscans exactly as the 1→1 playbook (full path always; basename always; ICASE / extension-less / URL-encoded per the host KB). Union the hit lists.
4. **Classify.** Verdict-log every hit per `classification.md`. One extra question per LIVE hit that the 1→1 playbook never asks: **does a successor exist?** Re-point live refs to the successor; where there is none, the fix is a supersession NOTE, not a re-point. Log which of the two each live hit gets.
5. **Execute.** History-preserving move into `{archive-container}/{batch-slug}/`, preserving the content's original relative layout below the batch directory. Add the `[ARCHIVED: date, reason, superseded-by?]` header to each archived file — header only, body untouched.
6. **Fix live refs** per step 4's re-point-or-note decision. Append-only operative records take append-fixes (never rewrite existing lines).
7. **Standing obligations** — none of these ever appears in the hit list:
   - Old parent manifest row → **ANNOTATE** (D1).
   - Batch manifest → **CREATE** per the host KB's convention (D2): thesis, date, reason, inventory, decision record, and any deliberate skips (e.g. Immutable bodies whose stale citations were deliberately left).
   - Archived node's own parent-pointer → **PRESERVE** (D3).
   - Stem-derived companions (sync snapshots, gitignored sidecars) travel WITH their main file. See § Companions.
   - **Outbound relative links inside the archived content** → recompute for the new depth (D4), then RESOLUTION-TEST each one.
8. **Symlink pass.** Whole-tree symcheck; delta against the preflight baseline must be empty.
9. **Verify.** Residue == logged leave-set. Every rewritten ref RESOLUTION-TESTED (a rewritten link is not a working link — see the 1→1 playbook's step-8 resolution gate). Plus the archive-specific gates:

Each gate is a COMMAND a fresh agent can run — not a description of one. `{area}`, `{batch}`, `{base-ref}` are yours to fill.

| # | Gate | Method |
|---|------|--------|
| 0a | **Decision record complete** | One row per decision unit; every verdict in the allowed set; every protected unit carries the protected verdict. A batch whose decision record is missing rows is a batch nobody can audit — and the rows you forgot are exactly the ones you did not think about. |
| 0 | **Protected paths still live** | `test -d` / `test -f` every path you promised NOT to touch. Run it FIRST — the cheapest way to catch a mutation that ran wider than its scope. |
| 1 | Live path vacated | `test ! -e {area}/{old-path}` |
| 2 | Batch complete | every archived unit present under `{area}/.archive/{batch}/` at its preserved relative path |
| 3 | File conservation | `git diff --name-status -M {base-ref}...HEAD` → renames only, **zero `D` entries** |
| 4 | No husk directories | snippet below — a directory left holding only a manifest and nothing else |
| 5 | No ignored-file leak | `leak="$(git diff --name-only {base-ref}...HEAD \| git check-ignore --stdin || true)"; [ -z "$leak" ]` — **`git check-ignore` exits 1 when NOTHING is ignored**, i.e. on the PASSING case, so a bare pipeline under `set -e` aborts on success. Capture the output and test it empty. |
| 6 | Headers + batch manifest | `[ARCHIVED]` header on every archived file; batch manifest present; Immutable bodies unaltered below the header |
| 7 | **Links resolve** | `scripts/linkcheck.sh <kb-root> <policy-file>` — compare against the pre-mutation baseline; the delta must be EMPTY (D4). **Status alone is NOT enough.** A checker that cannot RUN arrives as exit 1 under `set -e` (identical to "links found") and prints nothing, so a naive diff of two empty outputs reports clean. Assert the invariant: exit 1 MUST come with non-empty output, or the checker never looked. Use an ABSOLUTE path and an `[ -x ]` precheck. Covers both the archived content's own outward links and every inbound ref you rewrote. **A git-ref baseline compares TRACKED content only** — exclude gitignored trees from the delta or their pre-existing dead links all read as NEW. |
| 8 | Refs | `scripts/refscan.sh` per alias form → residue == the logged leave-set, set-equality both directions |

```bash
# Gate 4 — husk directories. TWO traps, both shipped live at least once:
#  1. `</dev/null` on the inner command: a command inside a read-loop that reads stdin EATS THE LOOP'S
#     OWN INPUT. (But NEVER put it on the loop's own input pipeline — that feeds the loop /dev/null and
#     silently disables it. Guard the commands INSIDE the loop, never the pipe feeding it.)
#  2. `if` — NOT `[ "$n" -eq 0 ] && echo ...`. A trailing AND-list makes the LOOP's exit status the
#     LAST iteration's test, i.e. "was the final directory a husk?" — so under `set -e` a normal tree
#     (last dir not a husk) returns 1 and KILLS THE GATE SCRIPT, skipping every check after it.
#     A gate that abort…2491 tokens truncated…cription alone; workspace precedent had in fact been fixing them. A directory whose name merely *sounds* retired — `.planning/`, `old/`, `legacy/` — is not a frozen container.)
3. **Navigation-pointer function test.** **SCOPE: this rule fires ONLY on a hit inside a FROZEN container (one rule 2 already froze).** It is the escape hatch out of rule 2 — nothing more. On a hit in an UNFROZEN container it does not apply at all; skip to rule 4. (Scoped 2026-07-13: as originally written its negative half — "body prose is a citation → historical" — silently fired on every unfrozen doc too, and since the lattice is first-match-wins it pre-empted rules 7-8 entirely, making them dead code. It froze exactly the files a live run had to fix.)
   **Append-only operative records are exempt from this rule.** If the frozen container is an append-only record (a log, a changelog, a run record — rule 4), a routing-shaped line inside it is STILL fixed append-only: add an old→new mapping line, never rewrite the existing one. Rule 4's entire purpose is that guard, and rule 4 sits BELOW this rule in a first-match-wins lattice — so without this exemption, rule 3 would emit `live, fix it` and the rewrite would falsify what the past run recorded. Same verdict, different fix: the fix is the point.
   **Machine-regenerated bodies are exempt from this rule, frozen or not.** If the hit sits in a body some pipeline re-derives (a sync snapshot, a compiled digest), a forward pointer inside it is fixed at the SOURCE and the body is never hand-edited — see rule 1. Rule 3 must never be read as licence to edit a generated body: a hand-edit there breaks the pipeline's own drift detection, and the next regeneration silently reverts you. (Restored 2026-07-13: scoping rule 3 to frozen containers accidentally dropped this, and a frozen snapshot containing "now lives at" then inverted to `live`.)
   Within a frozen container, for a NON-generated body: a line whose PURPOSE is routing today's reader OUT of the frozen record and onward to LIVE content — supersession headers, archive-README forward pointers ("Canonical:", "now lives at", "Relocated:", "superseded-by", a bare markdown link in a batch README pointing at the successor) → `live`; fix it even though its container is frozen. The label list is exemplary — function decides, not the label.
   **It must route OUTWARD.** A frozen manifest's own INVENTORY rows — the rows describing what sits beside it inside the batch — are not outward routing; they are the frozen record's description of itself, and they stay `historical` (this is what rule 2's "manifests included" means). The test: does this line send the reader to content that is still LIVE (→ fix it), or does it describe the frozen batch's own contents (→ leave it)? In-sentence mentions inside the frozen doc's body prose are citations, not routing → they stay `historical` (which is where rule 2 already put them; a dated briefing row-linked from a live INDEX keeps the doc reachable, but that does not make its inner narrative live — fix the INDEX row if the DOC moved, leave the prose). (Rule 1 cannot collide with this rule any more: rule 1 fires only OUTSIDE a frozen container, rule 3 only INSIDE one. A forward pointer inside an UNFROZEN generated body is rule 1's business — fix it at the source.)
4. **Append-only operative records** (error logs, changelogs, run logs that FUTURE runs consult as instructions) → `live`, but the fix is APPEND-ONLY: add an old→new mapping line; never rewrite existing lines.
5. **Live manifests and authority files**: INDEX.md (or equivalent) outside frozen containers; files the workspace policy names as live authority (records files, registries) → `live`.
6. **Sidecars** → `live`. A sidecar is a gitignored COMPANION whose name derives from its main file's stem (`{stem}.<class>.md` style) or that the workspace declares as a companion — it reconstructs its main file and must move with it (fix the reference AND physically move the companion). Every OTHER gitignored file is ordinary content: classify by these rules, fix its text in place, never relocate it just for being gitignored.
7. **Host-KB precedent** (checkable; use it before falling back to judgment). Does the KB's own record show how it classified THIS file — or this class of file — during a PRIOR mutation? Migration notes, historical-note blocks in manifests, and past batch READMEs routinely say so outright ("citations in X / Y / `dir/*.md` have been updated to point at the new paths"). If it does: **follow that precedent**, or overrule it explicitly and log why. A KB that treats the same file as frozen in one mutation and live in the next is incoherent in a way that neither choice alone would be — and the precedent is evidence about what the host KB considers a live pointer, which beats an outside guess. Absent any precedent, go to rule 8.
8. **Remainder** → judgment via the core test. The date on a document does not freeze it; what the path is DOING in the line decides:
   - **Communication / claim snapshots** (briefings, meeting notes, dated analyses, sent correspondence): body prose citing the old path is recording what was said or believed at a time → `historical`. Rewriting it falsifies the record.
   - **Working records of a program** (plans, progress logs, validation reports, deliverable inventories): the path is an ARTIFACT LOCATOR — it tells a reader where an output lives, and that output still exists under its new name. A reader follows it → `live`. The date stamps when the work happened, not what the file is called.
   - Where the two readings genuinely tie, prefer the one the host KB's precedent (rule 7) already chose; if there is none, prefer `historical` — over-fixing a citation is the more damaging error, because it destroys evidence, whereas a stale locator merely inconveniences a reader.
   - (Rule 3 is NOT in play here: it fires only inside a frozen container, and rule 8 is only reached for unfrozen hits. An unfrozen navigation line needs no exception — it is simply a live pointer.) Log verdict + one-line rationale.

## Self-reference

Two sources of designed self-hits. Both must be pre-logged BEFORE verify — an unlogged self-hit fails the residue gate.

1. **The run's own artifacts.** The verdict log and report cite old paths by design. If they live inside the KB tree, the verify-phase rescan hits them: pre-log each, verdict `historical`. (Better: keep them outside the tree, or `!`-exclude their directory in the policy file.)

2. **The run's own FIXES.** A correct fix routinely re-introduces the old path string. These are not residue to chase — they are the fix working as designed. Pre-log each. Four shapes, all observed in a single live run:
   - **Append-only mapping lines** (rule 4): the preserved original line still names the old path — that is the point.
   - **Strike-through resolutions**: a backlog or tracker item struck as done retains its original wording, old path included.
   - **Provenance notes**: an archive-batch manifest records what was migrated FROM.
   - **Migration / supersession notes**: a manifest or convention line that records the retirement necessarily names the retired path.

   The test: does this occurrence POINT a reader at the old location, or RECORD that the old location existed? Pointing → still a live ref, fix it. Recording → designed, log it and move on.

   **Verdict value for these rows: `live`.** They are hits that RECEIVED a fix — the fix simply happens to preserve the old string (that is what an append-only mapping line, a strike-through, or a provenance note IS). They are NOT `historical`: a historical verdict means "left untouched", and these were touched. They belong in the LEAVE-SET (the set of files that still contain the old path at the end) precisely BECAUSE their correct fix preserves it. Leave-set != historical + not-a-ref; see § Verdict log format.

## Verdict log format

| Path | Hint | Verdict | Rationale |
|---|---|---|---|

One row per hit; verdict values exactly `live` / `historical` / `not-a-ref` (append-only fixes are `live` with "fix: append" in the rationale). The log travels with the run report / commit body.

**The LEAVE-SET is not the same as the historical + not-a-ref rows.** It is every file that legitimately STILL CONTAINS the old path once the run is finished. That includes rows verdicted `live` whose correct fix PRESERVES the old string — an append-only mapping line (rule 4) keeps the original line verbatim; a strike-through resolution keeps the item's original wording; a provenance or migration note names what was retired. It also includes files the run itself CREATED. Build the leave-set explicitly, and gate residue as SET EQUALITY against it in both directions: an unlogged residue hit means a missed ref, and a leave-set file that no longer carries the old path means something was silently over-fixed. Both are failures.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# linkcheck.sh — resolve every relative link in a tree and report the ones that do not exist.
#
# Usage: linkcheck.sh <tree-root> [policy-patterns-file] [subtree]
# Output: one broken link per line, TAB-separated:  <file><TAB><link-target-as-written>
# Exit:   0 = no broken links, 1 = broken links found, 2 = usage.
#
# WHY THIS EXISTS.  A reference scan finds the old path STRING.  It cannot tell you whether a link
# RESOLVES.  Two failure classes are invisible to any text search, and both shipped on live content:
#   1. Rewriting a ref's path segment does not touch its `../` depth, so a "fixed" relative link can
#      still be dead — `](../x/y.md)` rewritten to `](../x/z.md)` is just as broken if the `../` was
#      wrong to begin with.  A live run found a template exemplar link that had been dead for months.
#   2. Moving content changes its ancestor depth, so every outward relative link inside it silently
#      mis-resolves with ZERO text change.  Nothing in the file differs; only where it sits.
# Run this after EVERY mutation, over the WHOLE affected tree — never scoped to the one file that
# prompted it (a file-scoped check goes green while its siblings stay broken).
#
# The gate is the DELTA against a pre-mutation baseline, not zero: most KBs carry pre-existing dead
# links, and fixing them is a different job from not breaking new ones.  Capture a baseline first:
#   LC=/abs/path/to/linkcheck.sh                       # ABSOLUTE: a relative path silently fails
#   [ -x "$LC" ] || { echo "not executable"; exit 1; }
#   run() { local rc=0; "$LC" . policy.txt > "$1" || rc=$?
#           if   [ "$rc" -gt 1 ];                  then echo "checker FAILED"; exit 1
#           elif [ "$rc" -eq 1 ] && [ ! -s "$1" ]; then echo "exit 1 but NO output -> not looking"; exit 1
#           fi; }
#   run before.txt      # BEFORE the mutation
#   # ... do the mutation ...
#   run after.txt       # AFTER
#   diff before.txt after.txt   # must be empty
#
# TWO TRAPS, BOTH PROVEN LIVE.
# 1. `|| rc=$?` is load-bearing.  Exit 1 ("broken links found") is the EXPECTED state on any real KB;
#    under `set -e` that status kills the script AT the linkcheck line, so `rc=$?` never runs and the
#    gate dies BEFORE the mutation.  `|| rc=$?` exempts it from `set -e` and captures the status.
# 2. A STATUS CHECK ALONE IS NOT ENOUGH.  A checker that cannot be EXECUTED (lost +x, bad interpreter,
#    wrong path) ALSO arrives as 1 under `set -e` (127 collapses), and it prints nothing — so before
#    and after are both empty, `diff` is clean, and the gate CERTIFIES A TREE IT NEVER LOOKED AT.
#    Exit 1 MEANS "links found": exit 1 with EMPTY output is a self-contradiction.  Test for it.
# CHECK THE EXIT STATUS.  Exit 2 = the checker itself failed (no python3, bad root, missing policy
# file) and it prints NOTHING — so a naive `diff` of two empty files is EMPTY, and the gate reports
# clean while the checker never ran.  That is a hollow green, and it CERTIFIES.  0 = clean,
# 1 = broken links found, 2 = the checker is broken.  Never conflate 2 with 0.
#
# STDIN HAZARD (this is why the loop below reads from a FILE, not a pipe into a while-read):
#   A command that reads stdin, placed inside a `while read` loop that has no explicit input
#   redirection, EATS THE LOOP'S OWN INPUT.  `rg` with no path argument is the classic case: it
#   searches stdin, consuming the rest of the loop's list, so the loop exits after one iteration and
#   every remaining item is silently reported clean.  This shipped once and scanned 1 of 25 paths
#   while the gate went green — a "hollow green" is worse than no gate, because it certifies.
#   Defences, all three used here: give every command an explicit path argument; add `</dev/null` to
#   any command inside a read-loop; and re-scan independently, in a fresh process, at the end.
#   Same hazard with ssh, ffmpeg, mysql — anything that reads stdin.
set -uo pipefail

usage() { echo "usage: linkcheck.sh <tree-root> [policy-patterns-file] [subtree]" >&2; exit 2; }
[[ $# -ge 1 && $# -le 3 ]] || usage
ROOT="$1"
[[ "$ROOT" != "/" ]] && ROOT="${ROOT%/}"
[[ -d "$ROOT" ]] || { echo "linkcheck: tree-root not a directory: $ROOT" >&2; exit 2; }
POLICY="${2:-}"
[[ -n "$POLICY" && ! -f "$POLICY" ]] && { echo "linkcheck: policy-patterns-file not found: $POLICY" >&2; exit 2; }
SUB="${3:-.}"
command -v python3 >/dev/null || { echo "linkcheck: python3 required" >&2; exit 2; }

# here (the historical HINTS are meaningless for link resolution). Without them, a tree the workspace
# has declared not-KB-content — an agent's own gitignored scratch dirs — floods the report with dead
# links you neither own nor should fix. On a real KB that was 142 phantom breaks against 250 genuine
# pre-existing ones: a gate that cries wolf is a gate that gets ignored.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# linkcheck.sh — resolve every relative link in a tree and report the ones that do not exist.
#
# Usage: linkcheck.sh <tree-root> [policy-patterns-file] [subtree]
# Output: one broken link per line, TAB-separated:  <file><TAB><link-target-as-written>
# Exit:   0 = no broken links, 1 = broken links found, 2 = usage.
#
# WHY THIS EXISTS.  A reference scan finds the old path STRING.  It cannot tell you whether a link
# RESOLVES.  Two failure classes are invisible to any text search, and both shipped on live content:
#   1. Rewriting a ref's path segment does not touch its `../` depth, so a "fixed" relative link can
#      still be dead — `](../x/y.md)` rewritten to `](../x/z.md)` is just as broken if the `../` was
#      wrong to begin with.  A live run found a template exemplar link that had been dead for months.
#   2. Moving content changes its ancestor depth, so every outward relative link inside it silently
#      mis-resolves with ZERO text change.  Nothing in the file differs; only where it sits.
# Run this after EVERY mutation, over the WHOLE affected tree — never scoped to the one file that
# prompted it (a file-scoped check goes green while its siblings stay broken).
#
# The gate is the DELTA against a pre-mutation baseline, not zero: most KBs carry pre-existing dead
# links, and fixing them is a different job from not breaking new ones.  Capture a baseline first:
#   LC=/abs/path/to/linkcheck.sh                       # ABSOLUTE: a relative path silently fails
#   [ -x "$LC" ] || { echo "not executable"; exit 1; }
#   run() { local rc=0; "$LC" . policy.txt > "$1" || rc=$?
#           if   [ "$rc" -gt 1 ];                  then echo "checker FAILED"; exit 1
#           elif [ "$rc" -eq 1 ] && [ ! -s "$1" ]; then echo "exit 1 but NO output -> not looking"; exit 1
#           fi; }
#   run before.txt      # BEFORE the mutation
#   # ... do the mutation ...
#   run after.txt       # AFTER
#   diff before.txt after.txt   # must be empty
#
# TWO TRAPS, BOTH PROVEN LIVE.
# 1. `|| rc=$?` is load-bearing.  Exit 1 ("broken links found") is the EXPECTED state on any real KB;
#    under `set -e` that status kills the script AT the linkcheck line, so `rc=$?` never runs and the
#    gate dies BEFORE the mutation.  `|| rc=$?` exempts it from `set -e` and captures the status.
# 2. A STATUS CHECK ALONE IS NOT ENOUGH.  A checker that cannot be EXECUTED (lost +x, bad interpreter,
#    wrong path) ALSO arrives as 1 under `set -e` (127 collapses), and it prints nothing — so before
#    and after are both empty, `diff` is clean, and the gate CERTIFIES A TREE IT NEVER LOOKED AT.
#    Exit 1 MEANS "links found": exit 1 with EMPTY output is a self-contradiction.  Test for it.
# CHECK THE EXIT STATUS.  Exit 2 = the checker itself failed (no python3, bad root, missing policy
# file) and it prints NOTHING — so a naive `diff` of two empty files is EMPTY, and the gate reports
# clean while the checker never ran.  That is a hollow green, and it CERTIFIES.  0 = clean,
# 1 = broken links found, 2 = the checker is broken.  Never conflate 2 with 0.
#
# STDIN HAZARD (this is why the loop below reads from a FILE, not a pipe into a while-read):
#   A command that reads stdin, placed inside a `while read` loop that has no explicit input
#   redirection, EATS THE LOOP'S OWN INPUT.  `rg` with no path argument is the classic case: it
#   searches stdin, consuming the rest of the loop's list, so the loop exits after one iteration and
#   every remaining item is silently reported clean.  This shipped once and scanned 1 of 25 paths
#   while the gate went green — a "hollow green" is worse than no gate, because it certifies.
#   Defences, all three used here: give every command an explicit path argument; add `</dev/null` to
#   any command inside a read-loop; and re-scan independently, in a fresh process, at the end.
#   Same hazard with ssh, ffmpeg, mysql — anything that reads stdin.
set -uo pipefail

usage() { echo "usage: linkcheck.sh <tree-root> [policy-patterns-file] [subtree]" >&2; exit 2; }
[[ $# -ge 1 && $# -le 3 ]] || usage
ROOT="$1"
[[ "$ROOT" != "/" ]] && ROOT="${ROOT%/}"
[[ -d "$ROOT" ]] || { echo "linkcheck: tree-root not a directory: $ROOT" >&2; exit 2; }
POLICY="${2:-}"
[[ -n "$POLICY" && ! -f "$POLICY" ]] && { echo "linkcheck: policy-patterns-file not found: $POLICY" >&2; exit 2; }
SUB="${3:-.}"

# has declared not-KB-content — an agent's own gitignored scratch dirs — floods the report with dead
# links you neither own nor should fix. On a real KB that was 142 phantom breaks against 250 genuine
# pre-existing ones: a gate that cries wolf is a gate that gets ignored.

EXCLUDES = []

"""Read-only Q07 probes against the actual retained APP-2026-001 projection.

Only in-memory copies of the application are varied. No batch processor runs,
no contract is changed, and no snapshot is created by these tests.
"""

from copy import deepcopy
import json
from pathlib import Path
import unittest

from jsonschema import Draft202012Validator, FormatChecker


ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]
WORKING = ROOT / "deliverables" / "working" / "batch-01"
APP_ID = "APP-2026-001"


class Q07Tests(unittest.TestCase):
    @classmethod
    def setUpClass(cls):
        cls.schema = json.loads((ROOT / "snapshot.schema.json").read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
        Draft202012Validator.check_schema(cls.schema)
        # Reference the unchanged contract's own definition; this is an
        # application compatibility probe, not a fabricated complete snapshot.
        cls.validator = Draft202012Validator(
            {"$defs": cls.schema["$defs"], "$ref": "#/$defs/application"},
            format_checker=FormatChecker())
        results = json.loads((WORKING / "results.json").read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
        cls.application = next(item for item in results["applications"] if item["application_id"] == APP_ID)
        cls.export_date = results["as_of"]
        cls.history = json.loads((WORKING / "history.json").read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
        cls.assessment = next(item for item in cls.history["applications"][APP_ID]["assessments"]
                              if item["as_of"] == cls.export_date and not item["historical_before_decision"])

    def test_actual_projection_has_missing_intake_without_recorded_dispatch(self):
        self.assertEqual(self.export_date, "2026-03-16")
        self.assertEqual(self.application["revision"], 1)
        self.assertEqual(self.assessment["intake"]["missing"], ["application signature and date evidence"])
        self.assertEqual(self.assessment["intake"]["notices"], [])
        index = [row for row in self.history["raw_tables"]["correspondence"] if row["application_id"] == APP_ID]
        self.assertEqual([row["document_path"] for row in index], ["decisions/2026-03-10_MEC-2026-011.md"])
        self.assertTrue(all(row["direction"] == "inbound" for row in index))
        pending = [item for item in self.application["action_queue"] if item["item"].startswith("Pending MSP dispatch")]
        self.assertEqual(len(pending), 1)
        self.assertEqual(pending[0]["owner"], "Medical Services Professional")
        self.assertIsNone(pending[0]["due"])
        self.assertIn("no response clock has started for these items", pending[0]["item"])
        self.assertFalse(self.application["packet_presentable"])

    def test_actual_null_status_fails_unchanged_enum_only(self):
        self.assertIsNone(self.application["status"])
        errors = list(self.validator.iter_errors(self.application))
        self.assertEqual([(list(error.path), error.validator) for error in errors], [(["status"], "enum")])

    def test_omitting_status_fails_required_contract_field(self):
        probe = deepcopy(self.application)
        del probe["status"]
        errors = list(self.validator.iter_errors(probe))
        self.assertEqual([(list(error.path), error.validator) for error in errors], [([], "required")])
        self.assertIn("'status' is a required property", errors[0].message)

    def test_inventing_pending_dispatch_status_fails_unchanged_enum(self):
        probe = deepcopy(self.application)
        probe["status"] = "pending-dispatch"
        errors = list(self.validator.iter_errors(probe))
        self.assertEqual([(list(error.path), error.validator) for error in errors], [(["status"], "enum")])

    def test_intake_incomplete_is_mechanically_valid_but_lacks_required_source_event(self):
        probe = deepcopy(self.application)
        probe["status"] = "intake-incomplete"
        self.assertEqual(list(self.validator.iter_errors(probe)), [])
        description = self.schema["$defs"]["application"]["properties"]["status"]["description"]
        self.assertIn("has been requested in writing", description)
        self.assertIn("the applicant's clock is running", description)
        self.assertIn("an intake status", description)
        self.assertIn("governs whenever a completeness item is missing", description)
        self.assertEqual(self.assessment["intake"]["notices"], [])
        self.assertTrue(self.assessment["intake"]["missing"])
        self.assertFalse(probe["packet_presentable"])
        self.assertIsNone(probe["approval_decision_id"])
        self.assertIsNone(probe["activation"])
        # Every other retained field remains unchanged by this probe.
        self.assertEqual({key: value for key, value in probe.items() if key != "status"},
                         {key: value for key, value in self.application.items() if key != "status"})


if __name__ == "__main__":
    unittest.main()
