def project(app, assessed, decisions, docs, reg, as_of):
    terminal, terminal_source = terminal_status(docs, app, reg)
    status = terminal
    missing = assessed['intake']['missing']
    notices = assessed['intake']['notices']
    active_requests = [n for n in notices if set(n['requested_items']) & set(missing)]
    if not status and missing:
        if any(n['returned'] for n in notices):
            status = 'returned-incomplete'
        elif active_requests:
            # Original request anchor never resets for partial/revised replies.
            # A fulfilled notice cannot expire newly identified, unrequested work.
            due = min(n['due'] for n in active_requests)
            status = 'ineligible-clock-expired' if as_of > due else 'intake-incomplete'
        elif all(n['request_coverage_known'] for n in notices):
            # Q07 owner exception: pending dispatch only, not an inferred clock.
            # Unknown notice coverage still needs review before classification.
            status = 'intake-incomplete'
    if not status and not missing:
        status = 'packet-presentable' if assessed['packet_presentable'] else 'in-verification'
        if any(not d['admitted'] for d in decisions):
            status = 'decision-inadmissible'
    approval, activation, conditions = None, None, []
    for d in decisions:
        f = d['fields']
        if not d['admitted'] or f.get('revision') != app['revision'] or f.get('body') != 'Governing Body':
            continue
        outcome = f['outcome']
        if outcome in {'approved', 'approved-with-conditions'}:
            effective = f.get('effective_date') or f['decision_date']
            end = appointment_cycle_end(effective)
            approval = f['decision_id']
            conditions = deepcopy(d.get('conditions', []))
            wa = assessed['licensure']['wa']
            if wa and effective <= wa['expirationdate'] <= end:
                condition = {'condition': 'Reverify Washington licence ' + wa['credentialnumber'] + ' before expiry; recorded due date is expiry under P Check 1.', 'due': wa['expirationdate']}
                if condition not in conditions:
                    conditions.append(condition)
            activation = {'active_at_export': effective <= as_of <= end, 'effective_date': effective,
                          'cycle_end': end, 'privileges': [x.strip() for x in f['privileges'].split(';') if x.strip()]}
            if not terminal and not missing:
                status = ('active-with-conditions' if conditions else 'active') if effective <= as_of else 'approved-not-yet-effective'
        elif not terminal and not missing:
            status = 'deferred' if outcome == 'deferred-pending-information' else 'denied'
    actions = assessed['action_queue'][:]
    for condition in conditions:
        if condition['due'] <= as_of:
            actions.append({'item': 'Unmet monitored condition requires Clinical Director review: ' + condition['condition'], 'owner': 'Clinical Director', 'due': condition['due']})
    if terminal:
        actions = [{'item': f'{terminal} recorded in {terminal_source}; retained unresolved evidence is historical, not active outreach.', 'owner': 'Medical Services Professional', 'due': None}]
    app_result = {'application_id': app['application_id'], 'revision': int(app['revision']), 'status': status,
                  'elements': assessed['elements'], 'packet_presentable': assessed['packet_presentable'],
                  'decisions': [{'decision_id': d['fields']['decision_id'], 'admitted': d['admitted'],
                                 'reason': d['failures'][0] if d['failures'] else None} for d in decisions],
                  'approval_decision_id': approval, 'activation': activation, 'monitored_conditions': conditions,
                  'action_queue': actions}
    return app_result


def process_batch(batch, sources):
    tables, as_of = batch['tables'], batch['export_date']
    reg = registry(sources)
    docs = indexed_documents(batch)
    results, history, packets, limitations = [], {}, {}, []
    for app_id in sorted({r['application_id'] for r in tables['applications']}):
        revisions = sorted([r for r in tables['applications'] if r['application_id'] == app_id and r['received_date'] <= as_of], key=lambda r: int(r['revision']))
        if not revisions:
            raise ValueError('No revision received by export for ' + app_id)
        app = revisions[-1]
        assessments = [assess(r, tables, docs, min(as_of, revisions[i + 1]['received_date']) if i + 1 < len(revisions) else as_of, reg) for i, r in enumerate(revisions)]
        current = assessments[-1]
        decisions, readiness_history = [], []
        for doc in for_application(docs, app_id, as_of):
            f = doc['fields']
            if not f.get('decision_id'):
                continue
            when = f.get('decision_date', '')
            if not when or when > as_of:
                raise ValueError('Decision date missing or after closed export: ' + doc['path'])
            candidates = [r for r in revisions if r['received_date'] < when]
            assessed_app = candidates[-1] if candidates else revisions[0]
            historical = assess(assessed_app, tables, docs, when, reg, before=True)
            failures = check_decision(doc, assessed_app, historical, reg, decisions)
            decisions.append({'fields': f, 'source': doc['path'], 'received_index': doc['index'],
                              'admitted': not failures, 'failures': failures, 'conditions': decision_conditions(doc)[0],
                              'readiness_evidence': historical})
            readiness_history.append({'revision': int(assessed_app['revision']), 'before_decision': f['decision_id'],
                                      'decision_date': when, 'presentable': historical['packet_presentable'],
                                      'outstanding': [x['detail'] for x in historical['issues']]})
        result = project(app, current, decisions, for_application(docs, app_id, as_of), reg, as_of)
        results.append(result)
        if result['status'] is None:
            limitations.append({'application_id': app_id, 'revision': int(app['revision']), 'code': 'Q07',
                                'detail': 'Required intake evidence is missing without an established applicable intake status; schema has no pre-dispatch status. Retained diagnostic file is held; pending dispatch/coverage review creates no invented clock.'})
        history[app_id] = {'revisions': revisions, 'assessments': assessments, 'decisions': decisions,
                           'readiness_history': readiness_history, 'current_revision': int(app['revision']),
                           'first_received_date': app['first_received_date']}
        packets[app_id] = {'revision': int(app['revision']), 'presentable': current['packet_presentable'],
                           'kind': 'revision-bound evidence summary; not a presentation event',
                           'source_documents': current['document_paths'], 'findings_and_work': current['issues'],
                           'requested': revision_rows(tables, 'privilege-requests', app),
                           'supported': current['privileges']['supported'], 'unsupported': current['privileges']['unsupported'],
                           'current_experience': 'Reserved to clinical leadership; criteria travel with the packet.'}
    observed_rules = {'B01', 'B02', 'B03', 'B04', 'B14', 'B15', 'B23', 'B24', 'B25', 'B26', 'B27', 'B28', 'B35', 'B36', 'B39', 'B40', 'B43', 'B44', 'B45'}
    for record in history.values():
        for assessed in record['assessments']:
            for item in assessed['issues']:
                observed_rules.update(re.findall(r'B\d{2}', item['rule']))
    return {'applications': results, 'history': {'raw_tables': deepcopy(tables), 'raw_documents': deepcopy(batch['documents']),
            'input_hashes': batch['input_hashes'], 'registry': reg, 'applications': history}, 'packets': packets,
            'limitations': limitations, 'rules_used': sorted(observed_rules)}
        raise InputError("Snapshot consumed inventory differs from opened batch inputs")
    if not (Path(root) / snapshot["rules_file"]).is_file():
        raise InputError("Rules register does not exist")


def _atomic_write(path, data):
    path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    temporary = None
    try:
        with tempfile.NamedTemporaryFile(dir=path.parent, prefix=".staging-", delete=False) as stream:
            temporary = Path(stream.name)
            stream.write(data)
            stream.flush()
            os.fsync(stream.fileno())
        os.replace(temporary, path)
    finally:
        if temporary is not None and temporary.exists():
            temporary.unlink()


def _sealed(path, root):
    name = path.relative_to(root).as_posix()
    result = subprocess.run(["git", "-C", str(root), "cat-file", "-e", f"HEAD:{name}"], capture_output=True)
    return result.returncode == 0


def run_batch(batch_path, sources_path, output_path, batch_number=1,
              schema_path="snapshot.schema.json", *, root=None, command=None, processor=None):
    """Consume batch 1 and write working evidence; never seal an occurrence."""
    root = Path(root or Path.cwd()).resolve()
    output = Path(output_path).resolve()
    if not output.is_relative_to(root):
        raise InputError("Output directory must be inside the repository")
    relative = lambda path: path.relative_to(root).as_posix()
    log = output / "run-log.md"
    written, consumed, batch = [], [], None
    timestamp = datetime.now(timezone.utc).isoformat(timespec="seconds")
    command = command or shlex.join([sys.executable, "-m", "credentialing", "run", "--batch", str(batch_path),
                                    "--sources", str(sources_path), "--output", str(output_path),
                                    "--batch-number", str(batch_number), "--schema", str(schema_path)])
    report = {"batch": batch_number, "outcome": "Blocked", "produced": written, "snapshot": None,
              "input_parsed": False, "contract_batch_complete": False, "diagnostics_retained": False}
    try:
        if batch_number != 1:
            raise InputError("G1 supports batch 1 only; continuation requires the next owner gate")
        batch = load_batch(batch_path)
        report["input_parsed"] = True
        consumed = [str(Path(batch_path) / name) for name in batch["input_hashes"]]
        sources, source_raw_hashes, source_text_hashes, source_manifest_hash = _load_source_capture(sources_path)
        consumed.extend(str(Path(sources_path) / name) for name in sources)
        if source_manifest_hash:
            consumed.append(str(Path(sources_path) / "manifest.json"))
        schema = Path(schema_path).resolve()
        consumed.append(str(schema))
        processor_hashes = _processor_hashes()
        rules_file = output / "rules.md"
        rules_hash = _sha(rules_file.read_bytes())
        consumed.extend([str(rules_file), *[str(Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent / name) for name in processor_hashes]])
        fingerprint = _sha(_json_bytes({"batch": batch["input_hashes"], "source_raw_hashes": source_raw_hashes,
                                        "source_text_hashes": source_text_hashes, "source_manifest_sha256": source_manifest_hash,
                                        "processor_hashes": processor_hashes, "rules_sha256": rules_hash,
                                        "schema": _sha(schema.read_bytes()), "batch_number": batch_number}))
        working = output / "working" / "batch-01"
        metadata_path = working / "run.json"
        snapshot_path = output / "snapshots" / "batch-01.json"
        if _sealed(snapshot_path, root):
            prior = json.loads(metadata_path.read_text()) if metadata_path.is_file() else {}
            if prior.get("fingerprint") != fingerprint or prior.get("snapshot_sha256") != _sha(snapshot_path.read_bytes()):
                raise InputError("Sealed snapshot cannot be overwritten; correction requires an authorized supersession")
            report.update(outcome=prior["outcome"], snapshot=relative(snapshot_path), unchanged=True,
                          contract_batch_complete=True, diagnostics_retained=prior.get("diagnostics_retained", True))
        else:
            if processor is None:
                from .engine import process_batch
                processor = process_batch
            result = processor(batch, sources)
            applications = result["applications"]
            if not applications:
                raise InputError("Engine returned an empty caseload")
            _validate_applications(applications, schema)
            expected = {row["application_id"] for row in batch["tables"]["applications"]}
            if len(applications) != len(expected) or {app["application_id"] for app in applications} != expected:
                raise InputError("Engine result does not preserve the complete, unique caseload")
            unrepresented = [app["application_id"] for app in applications if app.get("status") is None]
            limitations = list(result.get("limitations", []))
            if unrepresented:
                limitations.append({"kind": "schema-status-unrepresentable", "applications": unrepresented,
                                    "reason": "Computed pre-dispatch hold has no truthful status in unchanged snapshot schema; no contract snapshot produced."})
            outcome = "Blocked" if unrepresented else "Partial"
            report["outcome"] = outcome
            report["limitations"] = limitations
            if unrepresented:
                report.update(blocked_stage="snapshot-production", affected_applications=unrepresented,
                              error="Snapshot production blocked: application statuses cannot be truthfully represented in the unchanged schema; input parsed but contract batch incomplete. Diagnostic working results are retained, not a contract snapshot.")
            staged = {
                working / "results.json": {"batch": 1, "as_of": batch["export_date"], "applications": applications,
                                             "outcome": outcome, "artifact_kind": "diagnostic-working-results" if unrepresented else "working-results",
                                             "limitations": limitations, "rules_used": result.get("rules_used", [])},
                working / "history.json": result["history"],
                working / "packets.json": result["packets"],
            }
            metadata = {"batch": 1, "export_date": batch["export_date"], "fingerprint": fingerprint,
                        "input_hashes": batch["input_hashes"], "source_raw_hashes": source_raw_hashes,
                        "source_text_hashes": source_text_hashes, "source_manifest_sha256": source_manifest_hash,
                        "processor_hashes": processor_hashes, "rules_sha256": rules_hash,
                        "outcome": outcome, "snapshot": None, "snapshot_sha256": None,
                        "input_parsed": True, "contract_batch_complete": not unrepresented,
                        "diagnostics_retained": True}
            if unrepresented:
                metadata.update({key: report[key] for key in ("blocked_stage", "affected_applications", "error")})
            if not unrepresented:
                produced = [relative(path) for path in [*staged, metadata_path, snapshot_path, log]]
                snapshot = {"schema_version": "credentialing-snapshot/1", "snapshot_id": f"batch-01-{fingerprint[:20]}",
                            "predecessor": None, "batch": 1, "as_of": batch["export_date"],
                            "consumed": {"record_files": batch["record_files"], "documents": batch["document_files"]},
                            "produced": produced, "rules_file": relative(output / "rules.md"), "applications": applications}
                validate_snapshot(snapshot, batch, schema, root)
                staged[snapshot_path] = snapshot
                metadata["snapshot"] = relative(snapshot_path)
                metadata["snapshot_sha256"] = _sha(_json_bytes(snapshot))
                report["snapshot"] = relative(snapshot_path)
            elif snapshot_path.exists():
                raise InputError("An earlier unsealed snapshot exists; preserve it and resolve the changed input before producing diagnostic work")
            # Serialize everything before mutation; promote the snapshot last.
            staged[metadata_path] = metadata
            encoded = {path: _json_bytes(value) for path, value in staged.items()}
            for path in [item for item in encoded if item != snapshot_path] + ([snapshot_path] if snapshot_path in encoded else []):
                _atomic_write(path, encoded[path])
                written.append(relative(path))
            report.update(contract_batch_complete=not unrepresented, diagnostics_retained=True)
    except Exception as exc:
        report.update(outcome="Blocked", error=f"{type(exc).__name__}: {exc}", snapshot=None)
    report["produced"] = [*written, relative(log)]
    entry = {"execution_time": timestamp, "command": command, "batch": batch_number,
             "input_scope": {"batch": str(batch_path), "sources": str(sources_path), "schema": str(schema_path)},
             "export_date": batch["export_date"] if batch else None, "consumed": consumed, **report}
    prior_log = log.read_text(encoding="utf-8") if log.exists() else "# Run log\n"
    _atomic_write(log, (prior_log + "\n```json\n" + json.dumps(entry, ensure_ascii=False, indent=2) + "\n```\n").encode("utf-8"))
    return report


def main(argv=None):
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
    subparsers = parser.add_subparsers(dest="operation", required=True)
    run = subparsers.add_parser("run", help="consume one closed batch without sealing it")
    run.add_argument("--batch", required=True)
    run.add_argument("--sources", required=True)
    run.add_argument("--output", default="deliverables")
    run.add_argument("--batch-number", type=int, required=True)
    run.add_argument("--schema", default="snapshot.schema.json")
    args = parser.parse_args(argv)
    tokens = sys.argv[1:] if argv is None else argv
    try:
        report = run_batch(args.batch, args.sources, args.output, args.batch_number, args.schema,
                           command=shlex.join([sys.executable, "-m", "credentialing", *tokens]))
    except (OSError, InputError) as exc:
        print(f"Blocked: {exc}", file=sys.stderr)
        return 2
    print(json.dumps(report, ensure_ascii=False, indent=2))
    return 2 if report["outcome"] == "Blocked" else 0

## 6. Sealing, corrections and failure reporting

Before each sealing commit, check the candidate snapshot and working state together and record their actual paths. An uncommitted snapshot may be regenerated. Once committed, its occurrence is immutable.

For a correction to a sealed occurrence: retain its original bytes under a distinct archived filename; do the same for all superseded downstream occurrences; regenerate current standard paths with new snapshot IDs and correct predecessor hashes; document why and which occurrences were superseded; seal as a new commit. Unchanged reruns retain the existing snapshot and log the attempt without falsely claiming a new occurrence. A changed predecessor makes downstream replay necessary.

On a failure, report the attempted batch, command, execution timestamp, input scope, error and files actually written. Keep business unresolved work distinct from an unconsumable batch. Never label the earlier batch's snapshot as the result of a failed later run. Exact run-outcome reporting belongs in README and the run log because S has no run-outcome field.

def _atomic_write(path, data):
    path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    temporary = None
    try:
        with tempfile.NamedTemporaryFile(dir=path.parent, prefix=".staging-", delete=False) as stream:
            temporary = Path(stream.name)
            stream.write(data)
            stream.flush()
            os.fsync(stream.fileno())
        os.replace(temporary, path)
    finally:
        if temporary is not None and temporary.exists():
            temporary.unlink()

"""Synthetic decision records checked against the supplied standing registry.

These fixtures establish only the evidence they explicitly contain. No supplied
application batch is processed, and no synthetic record becomes business state.
"""

from pathlib import Path
import unittest

from credentialing.documents import parse_document
from credentialing.engine import check_decision
from credentialing.io import load_sources
from credentialing.policy import registry


ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]
EXECUTIVE = "Executive Committee of the Medical Staff"
GOVERNING = "Governing Body"


class DecisionTests(unittest.TestCase):
    @classmethod
    def setUpClass(cls):
        cls.reg = registry(load_sources(ROOT / "sources"))

    def setUp(self):
        self.app = {"application_id": "SYNTHETIC-APP-001", "revision": "2",
                    "first_name": "Test", "middle_name": "", "last_name": "Applicant",
                    "received_date": "2026-02-01"}
        self.assessed = {"packet_presentable": True}

    def document(self, **changes):
        body = changes.get("body", EXECUTIVE)
        role = next(item for item in self.reg["roles"] if item["role"] == f"Chair, {body}")
        fields = {"decision_id": "SYNTHETIC-MEC-001", "body": body, "signatory": role["name"],
                  "role": role["role"], "application": self.app["application_id"],
                  "revision": self.app["revision"], "decision_date": "2026-03-10",
                  "outcome": "recommended", "privileges": "PRIV-FM; PRIV-IM",
                  "criteria_version": self.reg["criteria_version"], "reason": "",
                  "effective_date": "", "supersedes": ""}
        fields.update(changes)
        labels = {"decision_id": "Decision ID", "decision_date": "Decision date",
                  "criteria_version": "Criteria version", "effective_date": "Effective date"}
        text = "# Synthetic decision fixture\n\n" + "\n".join(
            f"**{labels.get(key, key.capitalize())}:** {value}  " for key, value in fields.items())
        text += f"\n\nSigned: {fields['signatory']}, {fields['role']}, {fields['decision_date']}.\n"
        index = {"letter_id": "SYNTHETIC-LTR-001", "application_id": self.app["application_id"],
                 "date": fields["decision_date"], "direction": "inbound"}
        return parse_document("synthetic/decision.md", text, index)

    def failures(self, doc=None, *, app=None, assessed=None, prior=None):
        return check_decision(doc or self.document(), app or self.app, assessed or self.assessed,
                              self.reg, prior or [])

    def recommendation(self, **changes):
        doc = self.document(**{"decision_id": "SYNTHETIC-MEC-PRIOR", "decision_date": "2026-03-09", **changes})
        failures = self.failures(doc)
        return {"admitted": not failures, "fields": doc["fields"], "failures": failures}

    def approval(self, **changes):
        return self.document(**{"body": GOVERNING, "outcome": "approved", "decision_id": "SYNTHETIC-GB-001", **changes})

    def test_positive_recommendation_has_no_reason_requirement(self):
        doc = self.document()
        self.assertEqual(doc["fields"]["reason"], "")
        self.assertEqual(self.failures(doc), [])

    def test_unauthorized_committee_approval_retains_first_and_all_failures(self):
        doc = self.document(outcome="approved", role="Invented authority", revision="99",
                            criteria_version="INVENTED-VERSION")
        failures = self.failures(doc, assessed={"packet_presentable": False})
        self.assertTrue(failures[0].startswith("1 body/outcome authority"))
        self.assertEqual([item[0] for item in failures[:5]], ["1", "2", "3", "4", "6"])
        for body in [EXECUTIVE, "Credentials Committee"]:
            with self.subTest(body=body):
                self.assertTrue(self.failures(self.document(body=body, outcome="approved"))[0].startswith("1 "))

    def test_signatory_role_term_and_signature_are_verified(self):
        for doc in [self.document(signatory="An unlisted person"), self.document(role="Voting member"),
                    self.document(decision_date="2028-01-01")]:
            with self.subTest(fields=doc["fields"]):
                self.assertTrue(self.failures(doc)[0].startswith("2 signatory authority"))
        doc = self.document()
        doc["text"] = doc["text"].split("\n\nSigned:")[0]
        self.assertTrue(self.failures(doc)[0].startswith("2 signatory authority"))

    def test_wrong_revision_and_applicant_fail(self):
        for changes in [{"revision": "1"}, {"application": "SYNTHETIC-OTHER-APP"}]:
            with self.subTest(changes=changes):
                self.assertTrue(self.failures(self.document(**changes))[0].startswith("3 applicant/revision"))

    def test_missing_or_same_day_readiness_is_not_prior_presentability(self):
        self.assertTrue(self.failures(assessed={"packet_presentable": False})[0].startswith("4 prior presentability"))
        same_day_revision = dict(self.app, received_date="2026-03-10")
        self.assertTrue(self.failures(app=same_day_revision)[0].startswith("4 prior presentability"))

    def test_recorded_criteria_version_must_be_in_force(self):
        self.assertEqual(self.failures(self.document(criteria_version=self.reg["criteria_version"])), [])
        self.assertTrue(self.failures(self.document(criteria_version="LARK-PRIV-UNKNOWN"))[0].startswith("6 criteria version"))
        early = self.failures(self.document(decision_date="2025-12-31"))
        self.assertTrue(any(item.startswith("6 criteria version") for item in early))

    def test_governing_body_approval_requires_separately_valid_recommendation(self):
        approval = self.approval()
        self.assertTrue(self.failures(approval)[0].startswith("7 recommendation"))
        recommendation = self.recommendation()
        self.assertTrue(recommendation["admitted"])
        self.assertEqual(self.failures(approval, prior=[recommendation]), [])

    def test_invalid_wrong_revision_and_same_day_recommendations_do_not_substitute(self):
        invalid = self.recommendation(signatory="Unlisted chair")
        self.assertFalse(invalid["admitted"])
        wrong_revision = self.recommendation(revision="1")
        # Prior admission can be valid against its own older revision; it still
        # cannot authorize the current revision's approval.
        wrong_revision["admitted"] = True
        same_day = self.recommendation()
        same_day["fields"]["decision_date"] = "2026-03-10"
        other_app = self.recommendation()
        other_app["fields"]["application"] = "SYNTHETIC-OTHER-APP"
        for recommendation in [invalid, wrong_revision, same_day, other_app]:
            with self.subTest(recommendation=recommendation):
                self.assertTrue(self.failures(self.approval(), prior=[recommendation])[0].startswith("7 recommendation"))

    def test_duplicate_governing_decision_needs_explicit_supersession(self):
        recommendation = self.recommendation()
        earlier = self.approval(decision_date="2026-03-09", decision_id="SYNTHETIC-GB-EARLIER")
        previous = {"admitted": True, "fields": earlier["fields"], "failures": []}
        prior = [recommendation, previous]
        for supersedes in ["", "SYNTHETIC-UNKNOWN"]:
            with self.subTest(supersedes=supersedes):
                self.assertTrue(self.failures(self.approval(supersedes=supersedes), prior=prior)[0].startswith("8 duplicate/supersession"))
        self.assertEqual(self.failures(self.approval(supersedes="SYNTHETIC-GB-EARLIER"), prior=prior), [])
        # A second recommendation and a normal recommendation -> GB sequence
        # do not invoke the same-body Governing Body supersession rule.
        self.assertEqual(self.failures(self.document(), prior=[recommendation]), [])
        self.assertEqual(self.failures(self.approval(), prior=[recommendation]), [])

    def test_negative_outcomes_and_conditional_approval_require_reason(self):
        for outcome in ["denied", "deferred-pending-information", "approved-with-conditions"]:
            with self.subTest(outcome=outcome):
                doc = self.approval(outcome=outcome)
                self.assertTrue(self.failures(doc, prior=[self.recommendation()])[0].startswith("5 outcome/reason"))
                doc["fields"]["reason"] = "Synthetic recorded human disposition."
                if outcome == "approved-with-conditions":
                    doc["text"] += "\n## Conditions\n- Reverify licence by 2026-11-30.\n"
                self.assertEqual(self.failures(doc, prior=[self.recommendation()]), [])

    def test_unpublished_or_missing_privileges_are_refused(self):
        for privileges in ["", "PRIV-INVENTED", "PRIV-FM; PRIV-INVENTED"]:
            with self.subTest(privileges=privileges):
                self.assertTrue(self.failures(self.document(privileges=privileges))[0].startswith("5 outcome/reason"))

    def test_retroactive_effective_date_cannot_authorize_activation(self):
        failures = self.failures(self.approval(effective_date="2026-03-01"), prior=[self.recommendation()])
        self.assertEqual(len(failures), 1)
        self.assertIn("Effective-date backdate", failures[0])
        self.assertEqual(self.failures(self.approval(effective_date="2026-03-10"), prior=[self.recommendation()]), [])
        self.assertEqual(self.failures(self.approval(effective_date="2026-04-01"), prior=[self.recommendation()]), [])

"}

"""Extract labelled fields without allowing source prose to direct execution."""
import re
from .policy import normalized, person


def parse_document(path, text, index=None):
    fields = {}
    for line_no, line in enumerate(text.splitlines(), 1):
        match = re.match(r'^\*\*(.+?):\*\*\s*(.*?)\s*$', line)
        if match:
            key = normalized(match[1]).replace(' ', '_')
            if key in fields:
                raise ValueError(f'Duplicate field {key} in {path}:{line_no}')
            fields[key] = match[2].strip()
    return {'path': path, 'fields': fields, 'text': text, 'index': index or {},
            'title': next((x.lstrip('# ').strip() for x in text.splitlines() if x.startswith('# ')), '')}


def indexed_documents(batch):
    result = []
    for row in batch['tables']['correspondence']:
        path = row['document_path']
        result.append(parse_document(path, batch['documents'][path], row))
    return result


def for_application(documents, app_id, as_of, before=False):
    return [d for d in documents if d['index']['application_id'] == app_id
            and d['index']['date'] <= as_of
            and (not before or d['index']['date'] < as_of)]


def document_conflicts(doc, app):
    fields, conflicts = doc['fields'], []
    if fields.get('application') and fields['application'] != app['application_id']:
        conflicts.append('Document application differs from correspondence index')
    # Office correspondence commonly omits the middle name; preserve names,
    # accepting only exact first/last plus optional declared middle name.
    expected = {person(' '.join([app['first_name'], app['middle_name'], app['last_name']])),
                person(' '.join([app['first_name'], app['last_name']]))}
    for field in ('applicant',):
        if fields.get(field) and person(fields[field]) not in expected:
            conflicts.append(f'{field} identity conflicts with application: {fields[field]}')
    if fields.get('date') and fields['date'] != doc['index']['date']:
        conflicts.append('Document date differs from correspondence index')
    if 'period_explained' in fields:
        if fields.get('from') and person(fields['from']) not in expected:
            conflicts.append('Applicant explanation sender conflicts with application identity')
    return conflicts


def period(doc):
    match = re.fullmatch(r'(\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2}) to (\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2})', doc['fields'].get('period_explained', ''))
    return tuple(match.groups()) if match else None


def intake_notice(doc, app):
    """Recognize recorded MSP correspondence, not a pending action or interview promise."""
    if doc['index'].get('direction') != 'outbound' or document_conflicts(doc, app):
        return None
    text, title = doc['text'].casefold(), doc['title'].casefold()
    if 'medical services professional' not in text:
        return None
    returned = title.startswith('application returned as incomplete')
    if not returned and 'missing items on your application' not in title:
        return None
    match = re.search(r'(?:by|due on) (\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2})', doc['text'])
    # Recognize the supplied notice templates' explicit requests. Mentioning
    # an item elsewhere in a letter is not evidence that it was requested.
    requested = []
    if ('two items are missing from your application' in text
            and 'the larkhollow authorization and release, signed and dated; and a current curriculum vitae.' in text):
        requested = ['signed and dated Larkhollow release', 'CV present at submission']
    elif returned and 'please send a written explanation naming the period it covers, or a corrected application.' in text:
        requested = ['written explanation for every gap of at least 30 days']
    return {'date': doc['index']['date'], 'due_in_source': match[1] if match else None,
            'returned': returned, 'path': doc['path'], 'body': doc['text'],
            'requested_items': requested, 'request_coverage_known': bool(requested)}

"""Extract labelled fields without allowing source prose to direct execution."""
import re
from .policy import normalized, person


def parse_document(path, text, index=None):
    fields = {}
    for line_no, line in enumerate(text.splitlines(), 1):
        match = re.match(r'^\*\*(.+?):\*\*\s*(.*?)\s*$', line)
        if match:
            key = normalized(match[1]).replace(' ', '_')
            if key in fields:
                raise ValueError(f'Duplicate field {key} in {path}:{line_no}')
            fields[key] = match[2].strip()
    return {'path': path, 'fields': fields, 'text': text, 'index': index or {},
            'title': next((x.lstrip('# ').strip() for x in text.splitlines() if x.startswith('# ')), '')}


def indexed_documents(batch):
    result = []
    for row in batch['tables']['correspondence']:
        path = row['document_path']
        result.append(parse_document(path, batch['documents'][path], row))
    return result


def for_application(documents, app_id, as_of, before=False):
    return [d for d in documents if d['index']['application_id'] == app_id
            and d['index']['date'] <= as_of
            and (not before or d['index']['date'] < as_of)]


def document_conflicts(doc, app):
    fields, conflicts = doc['fields'], []
    if fields.get('application') and fields['application'] != app['application_id']:
        conflicts.append('Document application differs from correspondence index')
    # Office correspondence commonly omits the middle name; preserve names,
    # accepting only exact first/last plus optional declared middle name.
    expected = {person(' '.join([app['first_name'], app['middle_name'], app['last_name']])),
                person(' '.join([app['first_name'], app['last_name']]))}
    for field in ('applicant',):
        if fields.get(field) and person(fields[field]) not in expected:
            conflicts.append(f'{field} identity conflicts with application: {fields[field]}')
    if fields.get('date') and fields['date'] != doc['index']['date']:
        conflicts.append('Document date differs from correspondence index')
    if 'period_explained' in fields:
        if fields.get('from') and person(fields['from']) not in expected:
            conflicts.append('Applicant explanation sender conflicts with application identity')
    return conflicts


def period(doc):
    match = re.fullmatch(r'(\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2}) to (\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2})', doc['fields'].get('period_explained', ''))
    return tuple(match.groups()) if match else None


def intake_notice(doc, app):
    """Recognize recorded MSP correspondence, not a pending action or interview promise."""
    if doc['index'].get('direction') != 'outbound' or document_conflicts(doc, app):
        return None
    text, title = doc['text'].casefold(), doc['title'].casefold()
    if 'medical services professional' not in text:
        return None
    returned = title.startswith('application returned as incomplete')
    if not returned and 'missing items on your application' not in title:
        return None
    match = re.search(r'(?:by|due on) (\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2})', doc['text'])
    # Recognize the supplied notice templates' explicit requests. Mentioning
    # an item elsewhere in a letter is not evidence that it was requested.
    requested = []
    if ('two items are missing from your application' in text
            and 'the larkhollow authorization and release, signed and dated; and a current curriculum vitae.' in text):
        requested = ['signed and dated Larkhollow release', 'CV present at submission']
    elif returned and 'please send a written explanation naming the period it covers, or a corrected application.' in text:
        requested = ['written explanation for every gap of at least 30 days']
    return {'date': doc['index']['date'], 'due_in_source': match[1] if match else None,
            'returned': returned, 'path': doc['path'], 'body': doc['text'],
            'requested_items': requested, 'request_coverage_known': bool(requested)}

Check 3 — Professional education and post-graduate training
The manual, Section 6, Subsection 4, element 2:
"A qualifying degree is the degree required for the applicant's position and privileges."
"such as internship, residency, fellowship, or other organized professional training will be verified."
So: the qualifying degree, and every post-graduate training entry. The accepted sources are in attester-table.md. The admissibility rules are the ones in "What counts as a verification at all" above — the applicant may not carry the reply, and a source not on the table is raised.
The manual also states the boundary this check does not cross, Section 6, Subsection 4, element 2:
"obtaining a degree and postgraduate training does not automatically confer a license to practice"
Check 4 — Professional peer references
The manual, Section 6, Subsection 4, element 11:
"IHS policy requires the collection of at least two peer references at the initial appointment. The"
"All peer references are from a professional authority who has worked directly with the applicant within the past two years and can authoritatively speak to the applicant's character, clinical experience, and competency."
"the IHS definition of a peer includes a practitioner in the same clinical discipline."
"A peer must not be a relative, spouse, or partner."
Three disqualifiers, each independent: not worked together directly inside two years; not in the same clinical discipline; a relative, spouse or partner. A referee who fails any one of them does not count, and we find out only when the reply arrives and states the relationship.
Larkhollow rule — how each of the three is measured. The manual gives the conditions and not the arithmetic, so ours is:
* Worked together within two years is measured against the date the referee signs, because that is the day the referee attests to it. A referee whose last date working directly with the applicant is earlier than two years before their own signature date does not qualify. A blank last date means they still work together and the condition holds.
* Same clinical discipline is the discipline the referee states on the returned form against the discipline the applicant declared on the application. Both come from a fixed list.
* Relative, spouse or partner is the box the referee ticks on the returned form, read with whatever they wrote beside it.
Currency, from Section 8:
"Peer references are considered current if the reference's signature is within two years of the file presentation to the GB."
The signature date, not the date we received it. A reference can go stale while the file waits.
Larkhollow rule — when currency is measured. A reference is current when the presentation date is on or before the second anniversary of the signature date. For a file the Governing Body has decided, the presentation date is the decision date. For a file not yet decided, we measure currency against today, so that a reference about to go stale is visible before the committee meets rather than afterwards.
Larkhollow rule — the reference window. The manual states how many times to ask and does not state how long to wait. Ours: 21 calendar days per request, up to three requests. Request one goes out, request two 21 days later, request three 21 days after that. From day 64 after the first request the reference is overdue: we tell the applicant and ask for an additional referee. The original request stays open and stays outstanding; it is never closed as satisfied and never counted.
Larkhollow rule — the floor is two. Two qualifying, current references, both eligible on all three disqualifiers, both signed inside two years of the presentation date. An ineligible referee does not count towards the two even though the reply is in the file.
Larkhollow rule — an open request does not hold a met element. Once two qualifying, current references are on file, the peer-reference element is resolved. A request that is still open is carried on the action list until the file is presented and is then closed as no longer needed; it is never counted, and it does not hold the element or the file.
Check 5 — Board certification and the privileges requested
The manual, Section 6, Subsection 4, element 5:
"At the initial appointment, all active and inactive board certifications are verified."
"Verified through the certifying board."
All of them — a lapsed certificate is verified too, because what the applicant is certified in and what the applicant was once certified in are different facts and the file needs both.
On whether a certification supports a privilege, the manual gives the duty to clinical leadership:
"MSPs will check the facility's privilege criteria and conditions of employment (for IHS employees, review the position description, and for contractors, review the contract) to determine if the LP meets the board-certified/board-eligible requirements."
"The facility's clinical leadership is responsible for ensuring that the LP's board-certified or board eligibility aligns with the requested privileges."
and Section 9 says what criteria must address:
"At a minimum, privilege criteria should address the required education level, formal training requirements, and current experience."
Larkhollow rule — the criteria are published and versioned. privilege-criteria.md maps each privilege group to the certifying boards that support it and to a minimum training requirement, under a version string. Every decision record cites the criteria version it was decided under. The office applies the map; the office does not write it and does not extend it.
Larkhollow rule — name the unsupported subset. When some requested privileges are supported and some are not, the finding names the ones that are not. It does not reject the whole request.
Larkhollow rule — no supporting certification at all. When nothing the applicant holds supports any requested privilege group, this is an eligibility question, not a finding. The manual, Section 9:
"Threshold eligibility criteria are in place and consistently applied to each new applicant for medical staff membership and privileges."
"Do not accept applications for membership or clinical privileges from applicants who do not meet privileging"
"the clinical director will be consulted regarding discontinuing the application because the applicant doesn't meet the privileging"
The office raises it. The Clinical Director decides whether the application is discontinued.
Check 6 — The committee decision
Covered in sections 8 and 9.
4. High-risk findings
The manual, Section 7:
"A high-risk credentialing finding is identified as an applicant answering yes to any professional practice questions in "Table 1. Credentialing High-Risk Table" on an application."
"In addition, if any documents or verifications supporting the application illustrate that the applicant should have answered yes to a professional practice question but did not, the applicant is contacted to confirm the response."
Both halves apply here. A Yes on the disclosure page is a high-risk finding. So is a No that the evidence contradicts — a board record showing an action against a licence beside a No to the question about licence restrictions is the second half, and the applicant is contacted to confirm the response.
Larkhollow rule — where a high-risk finding goes. The Clinical Director is alerted, and the file is presented to the Executive Committee of the Medical Staff and to the Governing Body with the evidence. The manual's Section 7 also routes such a file to an Agency Clinical Credentials Committee for an endorsement determination; that body is a federal agency committee and there is no equivalent at Larkhollow. That route is out of scope for us. No third body exists here.
5. Privilege requests
Every application names the privilege groups it requests, from the current published criteria. The manual, Section 5, makes it a completeness condition:
"a request for specific privileges is received;"
An applicant may amend the requested set by submitting a revision.
6. Reserved judgments
Five judgments are not the office's and never become the office's, no matter how obvious the answer looks from the file.

def load_sources(path):
    """Verify captured bytes, then return UTF-8 text with any initial BOM removed."""
    return _load_source_capture(path)[0]


def _processor_hashes():
    package = Path(__file__).resolve().parent
    return {"credentialing/" + path.relative_to(package).as_posix(): _sha(path.read_bytes())
            for path in sorted(package.rglob("*.py"))}


def _validate_applications(applications, schema_path):
    schema = json.loads(Path(schema_path).read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
    Draft202012Validator.check_schema(schema)
    validator = Draft202012Validator({"$defs": schema["$defs"], "$ref": "#/$defs/application"},
                                     format_checker=FormatChecker())
    for app in applications:
        for error in validator.iter_errors(app):
            # Null is an explicit internal hold, never a public schema status.
            if list(error.path) == ["status"] and error.validator == "enum" and error.instance is None:
                continue

Five judgments are not the office's and never become the office's, no matter how obvious the answer looks from the file.
Judgment
	Whose
	Whether a gap explanation is satisfactory
	Clinical Director
	Whether a finding is disqualifying
	Clinical Director, then the Executive Committee of the Medical Staff and the Governing Body
	Whether to discontinue an application on eligibility grounds
	Clinical Director
	Whether to recommend appointment, and which privileges
	Executive Committee of the Medical Staff
	Whether to grant, modify, defer or deny
	Governing Body
	The office's job on each is to present the evidence the decider needs and to record the disposition that comes back. Presenting well is the work; deciding is not.
7. The Medical Services Professional's own role
The manual, Section 4, states it:
"verify, analyze, and prepare all relevant information regarding an LP's competency, character, training, experience, and judgment to present a complete and accurate file to the MEC and GB for recommendations and approvals"
8. Packet readiness
The manual, Section 12:
"It is recommended that every file be audited before it goes through review."
and Section 8, on how long a verification stays good:
"Most of these verifications are required by accrediting organizations to be verified AT the time of appointment, the time between when the application is received and when it's reviewed."
The manual gave a fixed number once and removed it: its own change log for Version 5.0 records "Section 8: Removed 120-day expiration of primary source verifications."
Larkhollow rule — the usability window. A verification is usable when it was completed on or after the date this application was first received and before the decision date. There is no day count. The anchor is the date revision 1 arrived, not the date of the current revision, so a later revision does not by itself void every verification already completed — what a revision invalidates is decided entry by entry, by reading what the revision actually changed. Peer references carry the additional two-year signature rule in check 4, which is stricter and wins where the two disagree.
Larkhollow rule — the board lookup and the window. A board lookup is the office's own check of the state board's public record on a day of the office's choosing, not a reply from a source, so the usability window is not applied to it: a lookup run on the decision day is usable for that decision. The date a packet became presentable is the date the last verification reply it needed was received; the lookup does not set it.
Larkhollow rule — what makes a packet presentable. Every one of the six elements resolved, no element outstanding, no discrepancy open, every verification inside the usability window, and the packet bound to one named application revision. Readiness is computed from the element statuses, not from anybody's recollection that the file looked finished.
For readiness, resolved means the element has nothing left to verify. An element carrying a finding is resolved in that sense once its evidence is with the Clinical Director — a licensure finding once the Clinical Director's disposition is on file, a certification finding on part of the request at once — and the packet is presented with the finding on it. An eligibility question, a gap awaiting the Clinical Director's disposition, an open discrepancy, an item returned to the applicant and a high-risk finding without its disposition are not resolved: while any of them stands, the packet is not presentable.
A packet is a statement about one revision at one moment. If any element re-opens, readiness for that revision is gone, and the earlier readiness record stays in the file as history.
Readiness is a fact about the revision's elements and nothing else. A refused decision record does not undo it, and a withdrawn or discontinued file keeps the readiness its revision had: the office records what was ready, whatever the file did next. Only an element re-opening or a new revision changes it.
9. The committee protocol
	What to do with a reply that is not on this table
1. Record it as received, with who sent it and how it arrived. Nothing is discarded.
2. Mark the entry still outstanding. An inadmissible reply does not resolve anything.
3. Keep requesting from a source that is on the table, and keep logging each attempt.
4. Raise it to the Medical Services Professional, who decides whether the case is one of the impossibility routes above.
Non-response is not impossibility. A source that exists and does not answer is a non-responsive source: it stays outstanding, the attempts keep being logged, and the manual's red flag applies. Only a source that no longer exists opens the secondary route.

def evaluate_privileges(app, tables, as_of, registry, entry_checks, before=False):
    """Preserve all received certification records; support requires verified facts.

    ``entry_checks`` are the evidence evaluator's current-revision checks. Only
    explicitly verified accreditation and accepted replies can establish training.
    Clinical experience requirements travel to leadership and are not applied here.

        result['issues'].append({'element': 'certification', 'kind': kind, 'detail': detail,
                                 'owner': owner, 'due': None, 'rule': rule, 'source_refs': refs})

    def current(row):
        return row.get('application_id') == app_id and int(row.get('revision', 0)) == revision

        rows = [dict(row) for row in tables.get('certification-replies', [])
                if row.get('application_id') == app_id and row.get('declaration_id') == declaration_id]
        check = {'declaration_id': declaration_id, 'declared': dict(declaration),
                 'verification_rows': rows, 'accepted_reply_ids': [], 'failures': []}
        result['certification_checks'].append(check)
        refs = ['declared-credentials.csv#' + declaration_id]
        for row in rows:
            # Future replies are retained as raw records and confer no knowledge.
            received = row.get('received_date', '')
            if not received or (received >= as_of if before else received > as_of):
                continue
            failures = []

                failures.append('Reply predates first application receipt')
            if not _accepted_source(row):
                failures.append('Source is outside the closed accepted-source table or is applicant routed')
            if row.get('board_code') != declaration.get('jurisdiction_or_board'):
                failures.append('Verified board does not match the declared board')
            if normalized(row.get('board_name', '')) != normalized(declaration.get('issuer', '')):
                failures.append('Verified board name does not match the declared issuer')
            if not row.get('certification_status') or not row.get('certificate_specialty'):
                failures.append('Certification status or specialty is missing')
            if failures:

                check['failures'].append('Latest same-day certification replies conflict')
                issue('outstanding', declaration_id + ': latest same-day certification replies conflict', refs, 'B20/B40')

"""Assess actual supplied application/CV documents, retaining comparison evidence.

Labelled Markdown is a supported input representation, not an office-mandated
form. Unrecognized representations stay outstanding for review. No attestation
substitutes for application signature or CV contents.
"""
from datetime import date
import re

from .documents import document_conflicts
from .policy import normalized, person
from .revisions import verified_role


def valid_date(value):
    try:
        return date.fromisoformat(value).isoformat() == value
    except (ValueError, TypeError):
        return False


def cv_rows(text):
    rows, headers = [], None
    required = {'entry', 'organization', 'role', 'from', 'to'}
    for line in text.splitlines():
        if not line.strip().startswith('|'):
            continue
        values = [v.strip() for v in line.strip().strip('|').split('|')]
        keys = [normalized(v) for v in values]
        if required <= set(keys):
            headers = keys
            continue
        if headers is None or all(re.fullmatch(r':?-+:?', v) for v in values):
            continue
        if len(values) != len(headers):
            return [], 'Malformed CV history row'
        rows.append(dict(zip(headers, values)))
    if not rows or len({r['entry'] for r in rows}) != len(rows):
        return [], 'CV history is absent, unsupported or has duplicate entry identifiers'
    return rows, None

              'cv': {'resolved': False, 'source_refs': [], 'comparisons': [], 'failures': [], 'conflicts': []}}
﻿Accepted sources by element — who may attest
Larkhollow Community Hospital · Medical Staff Office Table version LARK-ATT-2026.1, in force from 2026-01-01. Maintained by the Medical Services Professional.
The manual we adopted leaves its source lists open. Section 6, Subsection 4, element 2 ends "etc., as long as the source is a designated equivalent source for education and training verifications", and element 5 ends "or other nationally recognized certifying body, as long as the source is a designated equivalent source for board certification verifications".
Larkhollow rule. An open list cannot be applied the same way twice, so ours is closed. This table is the whole list. A reply from a source on it is admissible. A reply from any source not on it is inadmissible and is raised to the Medical Services Professional — it is not quietly accepted, and it is not quietly treated as a secondary source.
Two rules cut across every row, both the manual's, both from Section 6, Subsection 1:
"Primary source verifications received directly from the applicant cannot be used."
"Copies of a diploma, license, registration, etc., in place of verifications are unacceptable."
So the applicant is never an accepted source for any element, on any row below, however genuine the document they carry. The reply is filed as received and the request stays open.
Education and training
Class
	Accepted sources
	Primary source
	The degree-granting school's registrar's office or dean's office. The sponsoring institution's graduate medical education office or programme director, for a residency or fellowship
	Designated equivalent source
	Educational Commission for Foreign Medical Graduates (ECFMG). Federation Credentials Verification Service of the Federation of State Medical Boards (FCVS). American Medical Association Physician Profile. American Osteopathic Association Physician Profile. National Student Clearinghouse
	Secondary source — only on impossibility
	The applicant's most recent affiliation's medical staff office, stating how it obtained its own verification, when the school or programme has closed and no designated equivalent source holds the record. The reason is written into the file
	Not accepted
	The applicant. An alumni association. A departmental colleague writing in a personal capacity. A recruiter, staffing agency or locum tenens agency. A photocopied or scanned certificate from any hand
	Licensure

	Accepted sources
	Primary source
	The issuing state licensing board, through its own online verification service or a written reply from the board
	Designated equivalent source
	Federation of State Medical Boards Physician Data Center
	Secondary source

	Not accepted

+    conflicts = []

"""Record the supplied Clinical Director dispositions without making judgments.

Callers provide documents already limited to the relevant assessment date. A
valid disposition is retained even when its specifically referenced evidence
is missing; authority and evidence sufficiency are separate facts.
"""

from datetime import date
import re

from .documents import document_conflicts, period
from .policy import normalized, person


def _valid_date(value):
    try:
        return bool(re.fullmatch(r"\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2}", value)) and bool(date.fromisoformat(value))
    except (TypeError, ValueError):
        return False


def _sentences(text):
    # Only the narrative is scanned for explicit dispositions. Labelled fields
    # and headings cannot supply an instruction such as discontinuation.
    prose = "\n".join(line for line in text.splitlines() if not line.startswith(("#", "**")))
    return [sentence.strip() for sentence in re.split(r"(?<=[.!?])\s+|\n+", prose) if sentence.strip()]


def _authority(doc, app, reg):
    fields, index, reasons = doc["fields"], doc.get("index", {}), []
    for name in ("date", "application", "applicant", "recorded_by"):
        if not fields.get(name):
            reasons.append("Missing required disposition field: " + name)
    if index.get("application_id") != app["application_id"]:
        reasons.append("Correspondence application does not match assessed application")
    if not index.get("date"):
        reasons.append("Correspondence date is missing")
    else:
        reasons.extend(document_conflicts(doc, app))
    when = fields.get("date", "")
    if not _valid_date(when):
        reasons.append("Disposition date is not a valid recorded ISO date")
    role = next((item for item in reg["roles"] if item["role"] == "Clinical Director"), None)
    author = re.fullmatch(r"(.+),\s*Clinical Director", fields.get("recorded_by", ""), re.IGNORECASE)
    if role is None or author is None or person(author[1]) != person(role["name"]):
        reasons.append("Recorded by is not the rostered Clinical Director in that role")
    elif not _valid_date(when) or ((role.get("start") and when < role["start"]) or (role.get("end") and when > role["end"])):
        reasons.append("Clinical Director did not hold the role on the recorded disposition date")
    # The four supplied records use a standalone name and role as their footer.
    # A label claiming authorship alone is not the signed-record evidence.
    footer = [line.strip() for line in doc["text"].splitlines() if line.strip()]
    if (role is None or len(footer) < 2 or normalized(footer[-1]) != "clinical director"
            or person(footer[-2]) != person(role["name"])):
        reasons.append("Disposition lacks the rostered Clinical Director's name/role signature footer")
    return reasons


def _gap_evidence(app, doc, documents, gap, required_dates):
    qualifying = []
    expected_names = {person(" ".join([app["first_name"], app["last_name"]])),
                      person(" ".join([app["first_name"], app["middle_name"], app["last_name"]]))}
    for explanation in documents:
        index, fields = explanation.get("index", {}), explanation["fields"]
        when = index.get("date", "")
        explained = period(explanation)
        if (index.get("application_id") != app["application_id"] or index.get("direction") != "inbound"
                or not _valid_date(when) or when > doc["fields"].get("date", "")
                or explained is None or not all(_valid_date(value) for value in explained)
                or explained[0] > gap[0] or explained[1] < gap[1]
                or person(fields.get("from", "")) not in expected_names
                or document_conflicts(explanation, app)):
            continue
        if not required_dates or when in required_dates:
            qualifying.append(explanation)
    missing = [when for when in required_dates if not any(item["index"]["date"] == when for item in qualifying)]
    reasons = ["Specifically referenced applicant explanation missing or not qualifying: " + when for when in missing]
    if not required_dates and not qualifying:
        reasons.append("No qualifying applicant explanation covers the full disposed gap")
    return [item["path"] for item in qualifying], missing, reasons


def clinical_dispositions(app, docs, reg):
    """Return source records, authority checks, and narrowly explicit tags.

    `authorized` concerns roster/signature/identity/date only. `gap_cleared`
    additionally requires the recorded satisfactory judgment and every named
    explanation covering the entire disposed period. No tag verifies unrelated
    evidence, changes declarations, recommends appointment, or grants privileges.
    """
    records = []
    for doc in docs:
        title = doc.get("title", "")
        if not re.match(r"^Clinical Director['’]s disposition\b", title, re.IGNORECASE):
            continue
        if (doc.get("index", {}).get("application_id") != app["application_id"]
                and doc["fields"].get("application") != app["application_id"]):
            continue
        reasons = _authority(doc, app, reg)
        authorized = not reasons
        sentences = _sentences(doc["text"])
        terminal = any(re.match(r"^Discontinue the application\b", sentence, re.IGNORECASE) for sentence in sentences)
        amendment = any(re.match(r"^Offer the applicant the opportunity to amend the privilege request\b", sentence, re.IGNORECASE) for sentence in sentences)
        gap_match = re.search(r"\b(\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2}) to (\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2})\b", title)
        gap = tuple(gap_match.groups()) if gap_match else None
        evidence_reasons, paths, missing = [], [], []
        if gap is not None and (not all(_valid_date(value) for value in gap) or gap[0] > gap[1]):
            evidence_reasons.append("Disposed gap period is invalid")
            gap = None
        required_dates = sorted(set(re.findall(r"\bexplanation of (\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2})\b", doc["text"], re.IGNORECASE)))
        satisfactory = any(re.match(r"^(?:The )?explanation is sufficient\b", sentence, re.IGNORECASE) for sentence in sentences)
        if gap:
            paths, missing, gap_reasons = _gap_evidence(app, doc, docs, gap, required_dates)
            evidence_reasons.extend(gap_reasons)
        records.append({"path": doc["path"], "text": doc["text"], "topic": re.sub(r"^Clinical Director['’]s disposition\s*[—–-]?\s*", "", title, flags=re.IGNORECASE),
                        "date": doc["fields"].get("date"), "authorized": authorized, "reasons": reasons,
                        "terminal": "discontinued" if authorized and terminal else None,
                        "gap_period": gap, "required_explanation_dates": required_dates,
                        "ppq_codes": sorted(set(re.findall(r"\bPPQ-\d+\b", title + "\n" + doc["text"]))),
                        "amendment_offered": authorized and amendment, "gap_satisfactory": satisfactory,
                        "explanation_paths": paths, "missing_explanation_dates": missing,
                        "evidence_reasons": evidence_reasons,
                        "gap_cleared": bool(authorized and gap and satisfactory and paths and not evidence_reasons)})
    return records

# Escalation Requests

Commands are run outside the sandbox if they are approved by the user, or match an existing rule that allows it to run unrestricted. The command string is split into independent command segments at shell control operators, including but not limited to:

- Pipes: |
- Logical operators: &&, ||
- Command separators: ;
- Subshell boundaries: (...), $(...)

Each resulting segment is evaluated independently for sandbox restrictions and approval requirements.

Example:

git pull | tee output.txt

This is treated as two command segments:

["git", "pull"]

["tee", "output.txt"]

Commands that use more advanced shell features like redirection (>, >>, <), substitutions ($(...), ...), environment variables (FOO=bar), or wildcard patterns (*, ?) will not be evaluated against rules, to limit the scope of what an approved rule allows.

## How to request escalation

IMPORTANT: To request approval to execute a command that will require escalated privileges:

- Provide the `sandbox_permissions` parameter with the value `"require_escalated"`
- Include a short question asking the user if they want to allow the action in `justification` parameter. e.g. "Do you want to download and install dependencies for this project?"

## When to request escalation

While commands are running inside the sandbox, here are some scenarios that will require escalation outside the sandbox:

- You need to run a command that writes to a directory that requires it (e.g. running tests that write to /var)

When choosing a `prefix_rule`, request one that will allow you to fulfill similar requests from the user in the future without re-requesting escalation. It should be categorical and reasonably scoped to similar capabilities. You should rarely pass the entire command into `prefix_rule`.

- **Astra High:** lead orchestration, architecture, difficult policy/state/decision logic, integration, and final review. High is the ceiling; no Extra High.

def presentable(issues):
    # A partial certification finding is routed with the packet immediately.
    # Other unresolved work (including absent CD dispositions) still blocks.
    return all(item['kind'] == 'finding' and (item['element'] == 'certification'
               or item.get('clinical_disposition_sources')) for item in issues)


def decision_conditions(doc):
    """Read explicit dated conditions, preserving source wording and due dates."""
    section = False
    conditions, failures = [], []
    for line in doc['text'].splitlines():
        if line.startswith('## '):
            section = 'condition' in line.casefold()
            continue
        if section and re.match(r'^[-*] ', line.strip()):
            text = line.strip()[2:].strip()
            dates = re.findall(r'\b\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2}\b', text)
            if len(dates) != 1:
                failures.append('Condition lacks one unambiguous recorded due date: ' + text)
            else:
                conditions.append({'condition': text, 'due': dates[0]})
    if doc['fields'].get('outcome') == 'approved-with-conditions' and not conditions:
        failures.append('Conditional approval lacks parseable explicitly dated conditions; retain record for MSP review')
    return conditions, failures

## 6. Sealing, corrections and failure reporting

Before each sealing commit, check the candidate snapshot and working state together and record their actual paths. An uncommitted snapshot may be regenerated. Once committed, its occurrence is immutable.

For a correction to a sealed occurrence: retain its original bytes under a distinct archived filename; do the same for all superseded downstream occurrences; regenerate current standard paths with new snapshot IDs and correct predecessor hashes; document why and which occurrences were superseded; seal as a new commit. Unchanged reruns retain the existing snapshot and log the attempt without falsely claiming a new occurrence. A changed predecessor makes downstream replay necessary.

On a failure, report the attempted batch, command, execution timestamp, input scope, error and files actually written. Keep business unresolved work distinct from an unconsumable batch. Never label the earlier batch's snapshot as the result of a failed later run. Exact run-outcome reporting belongs in README and the run log because S has no run-outcome field.
